title.zh: 卷六十七 志第四十三 輿服三
title.raw: 卷六十七 志第四十三 輿服三 Volume 67 Treatises 43: Carriages and Clothing 3

sentences.zh: 文武官冠服命婦冠服內外官親屬冠服內使冠服侍儀以下冠服士庶冠服樂工冠服軍隸冠服外蕃冠服僧道服色

translations.literal: Civil and military officials' caps and robes; titled ladies' caps and robes; caps and robes for officials' kin inside and outside the capital; eunuch attendants' caps and robes; caps and robes for ceremonial attendants and those below; scholar-commoner caps and robes; musicians' caps and robes; military runners' caps and robes; foreign tributaries' caps and robes; Buddhist and Daoist vestments and colors
translations.idiomatic: Caps and dress for civil and military officials; caps and dress for titled ladies; caps and dress for officials' kin, inside and outside the capital; caps and dress for palace eunuchs; caps and dress for ceremonial attendants and those of lower rank; caps and dress for scholars and commoners; caps and dress for musicians; caps and dress for military runners; caps and dress for foreign envoys; Buddhist and Daoist vestments and colors

sentences.zh: 文武官朝服：洪武二十六年定凡大祀、慶成、正旦、冬至、聖節及頒詔、開讀、進表、傳制，俱用樑冠，赤羅衣，白紗中單，青飾領緣，赤羅裳，青緣，赤羅蔽膝，大帶赤、白二色絹，革帶，佩綬，白襪黑履。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials' court dress: Fixed in Hongwu 26 — for all great sacrifices, celebratory completion rites, New Year's Day, winter solstice, imperial birthdays, and the promulgation, opening and reading, presentation of memorials, and transmission of edicts — all used the beam-cap, red gauze upper robe, white gauze under-robe with blue-trimmed collar, red gauze skirt with blue border, red gauze knee-apron, great sash of red and white double-colored silk, leather belt, tassel sash, white socks and black shoes.
translations.idiomatic: On civil and military officials' court dress: In Hongwu 26 (1393) it was fixed that for great sacrifices, celebratory completion rites, New Year's Day, the winter solstice, imperial birthdays, and the promulgation, opening and reading, presentation of memorials, and transmission of edicts, all ranks wore the beam-cap, a red gauze upper robe, a white gauze under-robe with blue-trimmed collar, a red gauze skirt with blue border, a red gauze knee-apron, a great sash of red and white silk, a leather belt, a tassel sash of rank, and white socks with black shoes.

sentences.zh: 一品至九品，以冠上樑數為差。

translations.literal: From first to ninth rank, the difference lay in the number of ridges on the cap.
translations.idiomatic: From first through ninth rank, rank was distinguished by the number of ridges on the cap.

sentences.zh: 公冠八樑，加籠巾貂蟬，立筆五折，四柱，香草五段，前後玉蟬。

translations.literal: Dukes' caps had eight ridges, with cage-cap, sable cicada, standing brush five folds, four pillars, five segments of fragrant grass, jade cicada front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes wore caps of eight ridges, with cage-cap and sable cicada ornament, a standing brush folded five times, four pillars, five segments of fragrant grass, and jade cicada ornaments front and rear.

sentences.zh: 侯七樑，籠巾貂蟬，立筆四折，四柱，香草四段，前後金蟬。

translations.literal: Marquises had seven ridges, cage-cap sable cicada, standing brush four folds, four pillars, four segments fragrant grass, gold cicada front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Marquises wore seven ridges, with cage-cap and sable cicada, a standing brush folded four times, four pillars, four segments of fragrant grass, and gold cicada ornaments front and rear.

sentences.zh: 伯七樑，籠巾貂蟬，立筆二折，四柱，香草二段，前後玳瑁蟬。

translations.literal: Earls had seven ridges, cage-cap sable cicada, standing brush two folds, four pillars, two segments fragrant grass, tortoiseshell cicada front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Earls wore seven ridges, with cage-cap and sable cicada, a standing brush folded twice, four pillars, two segments of fragrant grass, and tortoiseshell cicada ornaments front and rear.

sentences.zh: 俱插雉尾。

translations.literal: All inserted pheasant tail feathers.
translations.idiomatic: All three ranks inserted pheasant-tail plumes.

sentences.zh: 駙馬與侯同，不用雉尾。

translations.literal: Imperial sons-in-law were the same as marquises, but did not use pheasant tail.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sons-in-law matched marquises but did not wear pheasant-tail plumes.

sentences.zh: 一品，冠七樑，不用籠巾貂蟬，革帶與佩俱玉，綬用黃、綠、赤、紫織成雲鳳四色花錦，下結青絲網，玉綬環二。

translations.literal: First rank: cap seven ridges, no cage-cap sable cicada; leather belt and pendant all jade; tassel sash used yellow, green, red, purple woven cloud-phoenix four-color brocade, knotted below with blue silk net, two jade sash-rings.
translations.idiomatic: First rank: a cap of seven ridges, without cage-cap or sable cicada; jade leather belt and pendant; a tassel sash woven in yellow, green, red, and purple cloud-and-phoenix brocade, tied below with a blue silk net and two jade sash-rings.

sentences.zh: 二品，六樑，革帶，綬環犀，餘同一品。

translations.literal: Second rank, six ridges, leather belt, sash-rings rhinoceros, remainder same as first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank: six ridges, leather belt, rhinoceros-horn sash-rings; otherwise the same as first rank.

sentences.zh: 三品，五樑，革帶金，佩玉，綬用黃、綠、赤、紫織成雲鶴花錦，下結青絲網，金綬環二。

translations.literal: Third rank, five ridges, gold leather belt, jade pendant, tassel sash used yellow, green, red, purple woven cloud-crane brocade, knotted below blue silk net, two gold sash-rings.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank: five ridges, gold leather belt, jade pendant; tassel sash in yellow, green, red, and purple cloud-and-crane brocade, tied below with a blue silk net and two gold sash-rings.

sentences.zh: 四品，四樑，革帶金，佩藥玉，餘同三品。

translations.literal: Fourth rank, four ridges, gold leather belt, medicinal jade pendant, remainder same as third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank: four ridges, gold leather belt, medicinal-jade pendant; otherwise the same as third rank.

sentences.zh: 五品，三樑，革帶銀，鈒花，佩藥玉，綬用黃、綠、赤、紫織成盤雕花錦，下結青絲網，銀鍍金綬環二。

translations.literal: Fifth rank, three ridges, silver leather belt chased with flowers, medicinal jade pendant, tassel sash used yellow, green, red, purple woven coiled-flower brocade, knotted below blue silk net, two silver-gilt sash-rings.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: three ridges, silver leather belt chased with floral designs, medicinal-jade pendant; tassel sash in yellow, green, red, and purple coiled-flower brocade, tied below with a blue silk net and two silver-gilt sash-rings.

sentences.zh: 一品至五品，笏俱象牙。

translations.literal: From first to fifth rank, all court tablets ivory.
translations.idiomatic: From first through fifth rank, all court tablets were of ivory.

sentences.zh: 六品、七品，二樑，革帶銀，佩藥玉，綬用黃、綠、赤織成練鵲三色花錦，下結青絲網，銀綬環二。

translations.literal: Sixth and seventh rank, two ridges, silver leather belt, medicinal jade pendant, tassel sash used yellow, green, red woven practice-magpie three-color brocade, knotted below blue silk net, two silver sash-rings.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth and seventh ranks: two ridges, silver leather belt, medicinal-jade pendant; tassel sash in yellow, green, and red practice-magpie brocade, tied below with a blue silk net and two silver sash-rings.

sentences.zh: 獨御史服獬廌。

translations.literal: Censors alone wore xiezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Censors alone bore the xiezhi emblem on their dress.

sentences.zh: 八品、九品，一樑，革帶烏角，佩藥玉，綬用黃、綠織成鸂氵鶒二色花錦，下結青絲網，銅綬環二。

translations.literal: Eighth and ninth rank, one ridge, black-horn leather belt, medicinal jade pendant, tassel sash used yellow, green woven xichi two-color brocade, knotted below blue silk net, two copper sash-rings.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth and ninth ranks: one ridge, black-horn leather belt, medicinal-jade pendant; tassel sash in yellow and green xichi brocade, tied below with a blue silk net and two copper sash-rings.

sentences.zh: 六品至九品，笏俱槐木。

translations.literal: From sixth to ninth rank, all court tablets locust wood.
translations.idiomatic: From sixth through ninth rank, all court tablets were of locust wood.

sentences.zh: 其武官應直守衛者，別有服色。

translations.literal: Military officers on duty guard had separate dress colors.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers on rotating guard duty had separate dress colors.

sentences.zh: 雜職未入流品者，大朝賀、進錶行禮止用公服。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous posts not entered into the rank stream, for great court congratulations and presenting memorials performing rites used only service dress.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous posts outside the rank stream used only service dress for great court congratulations and the presentation of memorials.

sentences.zh: 三十年令視九品官，用朝服。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year an order treated them as ninth-rank officials, using court dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Hongwu they were ordered to be treated as ninth-rank officials and to wear court dress.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年，更定朝服之制。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 8, the court dress system was revised.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 8 (1529) the regulations for court dress were revised.

sentences.zh: 樑冠如舊式，上衣赤羅青緣，長過腰指七寸，毋掩下裳。

translations.literal: Beam-cap as old style; upper robe red gauze blue border, length past waist seven inches, must not cover lower skirt.
translations.idiomatic: The beam-cap followed the old style; the upper robe was red gauze with blue border, seven inches below the waist and not to cover the lower skirt.

sentences.zh: 中單白紗青緣。

translations.literal: Under-robe white gauze blue border.
translations.idiomatic: The under-robe was white gauze with blue border.

sentences.zh: 下裳七幅，前三後四，每幅三襞積，赤羅青緣。

translations.literal: Lower skirt seven panels, three front four rear, each panel three pleats, red gauze blue border.
translations.idiomatic: The lower skirt had seven panels—three in front and four behind—with three pleats per panel, in red gauze with blue border.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝綴革帶。

translations.literal: Knee-apron attached to leather belt.
translations.idiomatic: The knee-apron was fastened to the leather belt.

sentences.zh: 綬，各從品級花樣。

translations.literal: Tassel sash, each according to rank pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The tassel sash followed each rank's prescribed pattern.

sentences.zh: 革帶之後佩綬，系而掩之。

translations.literal: Behind the leather belt hung the tassel sash, tied and covered over.
translations.idiomatic: The tassel sash hung behind the leather belt, tied and folded under it.

sentences.zh: 其環亦各從品級，用玉犀金銀銅，不以織於綬。

translations.literal: Its rings also each according to rank, used jade rhinoceros gold silver copper, not woven into the sash.
translations.idiomatic: The sash-rings likewise followed rank, in jade, rhinoceros horn, gold, silver, or copper, and were no longer woven into the sash itself.

sentences.zh: 大帶表裏俱素，惟兩耳及下垂緣綠，又以青組約之。

translations.literal: Great sash inside and outside all plain, only the two ears and hanging border green, also bound with blue cord.
translations.idiomatic: The great sash was plain inside and out, with green only on the two ears and the hanging border, and was bound with blue cord.

sentences.zh: 革帶俱如舊式。

translations.literal: Leather belts all as old style.
translations.idiomatic: Leather belts remained as in the old style.

sentences.zh: 珮玉一如《詩傳》之制，去雙滴及二珩。

translations.literal: Jade pendants exactly as in the Classic of Poetry commentary system, removing double drops and two top pendants.
translations.idiomatic: Jade pendants followed the system in the Classic of Poetry commentary, omitting the double drops and the two top pendants.

sentences.zh: 其三品以上玉，四品以下藥玉，及襪履俱如舊式。

translations.literal: Third rank and above jade, fourth rank and below medicinal jade, and socks shoes all as old style.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above wore jade; fourth rank and below wore medicinal jade; socks and shoes remained as before.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年，令百官正旦朝賀毋僭躡硃履。

translations.literal: Wanli 5, ordered all officials at New Year's court congratulations not to usurp wearing vermilion shoes.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 5 (1577) officials were forbidden to wear vermilion shoes at the New Year's court congratulations.

sentences.zh: 故事，十一月百官戴暖耳。

translations.literal: Precedent: in the eleventh month all officials wore warm ear-covers.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, in the eleventh month all officials wore warm ear-covers.

sentences.zh: 是年朝覲外官及舉人、監生，不許戴暖耳入朝。

translations.literal: That year officials from outside attending court and examination graduates and students, not permitted to wear warm ear-covers entering court.
translations.idiomatic: That year officials from the provinces attending court, together with examination graduates and students, were forbidden to wear warm ear-covers in court.

sentences.zh: 凡親祀郊廟、社稷，文武官分獻陪祀，則服祭服。

translations.literal: Whenever personally sacrificing at suburban altars and temples, soil and grain, civil and military officials dividing offerings and accompanying sacrifice, then wore sacrificial dress.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor personally sacrificed at the suburban altars, the ancestral temples, or the altars of soil and grain, civil and military officials who divided offerings or accompanied the rite wore sacrificial dress.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年定，一品至九品，青羅衣，白紗中單，俱皁領緣。

translations.literal: Fixed in Hongwu 26, first to ninth rank, blue gauze upper robe, white gauze under-robe, all black collar border.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed in Hongwu 26: from first through ninth rank, a blue gauze upper robe and white gauze under-robe, both with black-trimmed collars.

sentences.zh: 赤羅裳，皁緣。

translations.literal: Red gauze skirt, black border.
translations.idiomatic: A red gauze skirt with black border.

sentences.zh: 赤羅蔽膝。

translations.literal: Red gauze knee-apron.
translations.idiomatic: A red gauze knee-apron.

sentences.zh: 方心曲領。

translations.literal: Square-heart curved collar.
translations.idiomatic: A square-heart curved collar-piece.

sentences.zh: 其冠帶、佩綬等差，並同朝服。

translations.literal: Their caps, belts, pendant tassel sash gradations, all same as court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Caps, belts, pendants, and tassel sashes followed the same gradations as court dress.

sentences.zh: 又定品官家用祭服。

translations.literal: Also fixed ranked officials' household sacrificial dress.
translations.idiomatic: Household sacrificial dress for ranked officials was also fixed.

sentences.zh: 三品以上，去方心曲領。

translations.literal: Third rank and above, removed square-heart curved collar.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above omitted the square-heart curved collar.

sentences.zh: 四品以下，並去珮綬。

translations.literal: Fourth rank and below, all removed pendant tassel sash.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank and below omitted both pendant and tassel sash.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年，更定百官祭服。

translations.literal: Jiajing 8, revised all officials' sacrificial dress.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 8 the sacrificial dress of all officials was revised.

sentences.zh: 上衣青羅，皁緣，與朝服同。

translations.literal: Upper robe blue gauze, black border, same as court dress.
translations.idiomatic: The upper robe was blue gauze with black border, as in court dress.

sentences.zh: 下裳赤羅，皁緣，與朝服同。

translations.literal: Lower skirt red gauze, black border, same as court dress.
translations.idiomatic: The lower skirt was red gauze with black border, as in court dress.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝、綬環、大帶、革帶、佩玉、襪履俱與朝服同。

translations.literal: Knee-apron, sash-rings, great sash, leather belt, jade pendant, socks shoes all same as court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Knee-apron, sash-rings, great sash, leather belt, jade pendant, socks, and shoes all matched court dress.

sentences.zh: 其視牲、朝日夕月、耕耤、祭歷代帝王，獨錦衣衛堂上官，大紅蟒衣，飛魚，烏紗帽，鸞帶，佩繡春刀。

translations.literal: For inspecting victims, morning sun evening moon, ploughing sacred field, sacrificing to successive dynasties' emperors, only Brocade-Guard senior hall officials, great red python robe, flying fish, black gauze cap, luan belt, wore embroidered spring knife.
translations.idiomatic: For inspecting sacrificial victims, the rites of the morning sun and evening moon, the sacred ploughing, and sacrifices to successive dynasties' emperors, only senior Brocade Guard hall officers wore great red python robes with flying-fish designs, black gauze caps, luan belts, and embroidered spring knives at the belt.

sentences.zh: 祭太廟、社稷，則大紅便服。

translations.literal: Sacrificing at Grand Temple, soil and grain, then great red informal dress.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices at the Grand Temple and the altars of soil and grain they wore great red informal dress.

sentences.zh: 文武官公服：洪武二十六年定，每日早晚朝奏事及侍班、謝恩、見辭則服之。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials' service dress: Fixed Hongwu 26, daily morning and evening court presenting affairs and attending roster, thanking grace, farewell audience then wore it.
translations.idiomatic: On civil and military officials' service dress: Fixed in Hongwu 26, it was worn for daily morning and evening audiences, presenting business at court, attending roster duty, thanking for grace, and farewell audiences.

sentences.zh: 在外文武官，每日公座服之。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials outside the capital, daily at official seat wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials outside the capital wore it daily at their official seats.

sentences.zh: 其制，盤領右衽袍，用紵絲或紗羅絹，袖寬三尺。

translations.literal: Its form: round collar right-lapel robe, used ramie silk or gauze silk satin, sleeves wide three feet.
translations.idiomatic: The garment was a round-collared, right-lapped robe of ramie silk, gauze, silk, or satin, with sleeves three feet wide.

sentences.zh: 一品至四品，緋袍；

translations.literal: First to fourth rank, scarlet robe;
translations.idiomatic: First through fourth ranks wore scarlet robes;

sentences.zh: 五品至七品，青袍；

translations.literal: Fifth to seventh rank, blue robe;
translations.idiomatic: fifth through seventh ranks wore blue robes;

sentences.zh: 八品九品，綠袍；

translations.literal: Eighth ninth rank, green robe;
translations.idiomatic: eighth and ninth ranks wore green robes;

sentences.zh: 未入流雜職官，袍、笏、帶與八品以下同。

translations.literal: Not entered stream miscellaneous posts, robe tablet belt same as eighth rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: miscellaneous posts outside the rank stream used the same robe, tablet, and belt as eighth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 公服花樣，一品，大獨科花，徑五寸；

translations.literal: Service dress patterns, first rank, large single-branch flower, diameter five inches;
translations.idiomatic: Service-dress patterns: first rank, large single-branch flowers five inches across;

sentences.zh: 二品，小獨科花，徑三寸；

translations.literal: Second rank, small single-branch flower, diameter three inches;
translations.idiomatic: second rank, small single-branch flowers three inches across;

sentences.zh: 三品，散答花，無枝葉，徑二寸；

translations.literal: Third rank, scattered answering flowers, no branches leaves, diameter two inches;
translations.idiomatic: third rank, scattered floral roundels without branches or leaves, two inches across;

sentences.zh: 四品、五品，小雜花紋，徑一寸五分；

translations.literal: Fourth fifth rank, small mixed flower pattern, diameter one inch five fen;
translations.idiomatic: fourth and fifth ranks, small mixed floral patterns one and a half inches across;

sentences.zh: 六品、七品，小雜花，徑一寸；

translations.literal: Sixth seventh rank, small mixed flowers, diameter one inch;
translations.idiomatic: sixth and seventh ranks, small mixed flowers one inch across;

sentences.zh: 八品以下無紋。

translations.literal: Eighth rank and below no pattern.
translations.idiomatic: eighth rank and below had no pattern.

sentences.zh: 襆頭：漆、紗二等，展角長一尺二寸；

translations.literal: Futou: lacquer, gauze two grades, spread corners length one foot two inches;
translations.idiomatic: Futou headwraps came in lacquered and gauze types, with spread corners one foot two inches long;

sentences.zh: 雜職官襆頭，垂帶，後復令展角，不用垂帶，與入流官同。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous posts' futou, hanging ribbons, later again ordered spread corners, not use hanging ribbons, same as entered-stream officials.
translations.idiomatic: miscellaneous posts had originally worn futou with hanging ribbons, but were later ordered to use spread corners without ribbons, the same as ranked officials.

sentences.zh: 笏依朝服為之。

translations.literal: Court tablet according to court dress made.
translations.idiomatic: Court tablets followed the court-dress regulations.

sentences.zh: 腰帶：一品玉，或花或素；

translations.literal: Waist belt: first rank jade, either patterned or plain;
translations.idiomatic: Waist belts: first rank, jade, patterned or plain;

sentences.zh: 二品犀；

translations.literal: Second rank rhinoceros;
translations.idiomatic: second rank, rhinoceros horn;

sentences.zh: 三品、四品，金荔枝；

translations.literal: Third fourth rank, gold lychee;
translations.idiomatic: third and fourth ranks, gold with lychee design;

sentences.zh: 五品以下烏角。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and below black horn.
translations.idiomatic: fifth rank and below, black horn.

sentences.zh: 襪用青革，仍垂撻尾於下。

translations.literal: Socks used blue leather, still hung tassel tails below.
translations.idiomatic: Socks were of blue leather, with tassel tails still hanging below.

sentences.zh: 靴用皁。

translations.literal: Boots used black.
translations.idiomatic: Boots were black.

sentences.zh: 其後，常朝止便服，惟朔望具公服朝參。

translations.literal: Afterward, regular court stopped at informal dress, only new and full moon fully equipped service dress court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Later, regular audiences required only informal dress; service dress was worn fully only on the first and fifteenth of the month.

sentences.zh: 凡武官應直守衛者，別有服色，不拘此制。

translations.literal: All military officers on rotating guard, separate dress colors, not bound by this system.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers on rotating guard had separate colors and were not bound by this rule.

sentences.zh: 公、侯、駙馬、伯服色花樣、腰帶與一品同。

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, earls dress colors patterns waist belts same as first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, and earls used the same colors, patterns, and waist belts as first rank.

sentences.zh: 文武官花樣，如無從織造，則用素。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials' patterns, if no means to weave, then used plain.
translations.idiomatic: If officials could not obtain woven patterns, they wore plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 百官入朝，雨雪許服雨衣。

translations.literal: All officials entering court, in rain snow permitted to wear rain coats.
translations.idiomatic: Officials entering court in rain or snow were permitted rain cloaks.

sentences.zh: 奉天、華蓋、武英諸殿奏事，必躡履鞋，違者御史糾之。

translations.literal: Fengtian, Huagai, Wuying various halls presenting business, must tread soft-sole shoes, violators censors impeached.
translations.idiomatic: When presenting business in the Fengtian, Huagai, and Wuying halls, officials had to wear soft-sole court shoes; violators were impeached by the censors.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年，令常朝俱衣本等錦繡服色，其朝覲官見辭、謝恩，不論已未入流，公服行禮。

translations.literal: Wanli 5, ordered regular court all wear their rank brocade embroidered colors, officials from outside farewell thanking grace, regardless entered or not entered stream, service dress perform rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 5 regular audiences required each rank's brocade colors; for farewell and thanksgiving audiences, whether inside or outside the rank stream, service dress was used.

sentences.zh: 文武官常服：洪武三年定，凡常朝視事，以烏紗帽、團領衫、束帶為公服。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials' regular dress: Fixed Hongwu 3, all regular court viewing affairs, used black gauze cap, round-collar robe, bound belt as service dress.
translations.idiomatic: On civil and military officials' regular dress: Fixed in Hongwu 3, for regular audiences and daily business the black gauze cap, round-collared robe, and bound belt served as everyday dress.

sentences.zh: 其帶，一品玉，二品花犀，三品金鈒花，四品素金，五品銀鈒花，六品、七品素銀，八品、九品烏角。

translations.literal: Its belts, first rank jade, second rank patterned rhinoceros, third rank gold chased flowers, fourth rank plain gold, fifth rank silver chased flowers, sixth seventh plain silver, eighth ninth black horn.
translations.idiomatic: Belts: first rank jade; second rank patterned rhinoceros horn; third rank gold chased with flowers; fourth rank plain gold; fifth rank silver chased with flowers; sixth and seventh ranks plain silver; eighth and ninth ranks black horn.

sentences.zh: 凡致仕及侍親辭閑官，紗帽、束帶。

translations.literal: All retired and attending kin leaving idle posts, gauze cap, bound belt.
translations.idiomatic: Retired officials and those leaving office to attend kin wore gauze caps and bound belts.

sentences.zh: 為事黜降者，服與庶人同。

translations.literal: Demoted for affairs, dress same as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Those demoted for misconduct dressed as commoners.

sentences.zh: 至二十四年，又定公、侯、伯、駙馬束帶與一品同，雜職官與八品、九品同。

translations.literal: By the twenty-fourth year, again fixed dukes marquises earls imperial sons-in-law bound belts same as first rank, miscellaneous posts same as eighth ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year it was further fixed that dukes, marquises, earls, and imperial sons-in-law used the same belts as first rank, and miscellaneous posts the same as eighth and ninth ranks.

sentences.zh: 朝官常服禮鞋，洪武六年定。

translations.literal: Court officials' regular dress ceremonial shoes, fixed Hongwu 6.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial shoes for officials' regular dress were fixed in Hongwu 6.

sentences.zh: 先是，百官入朝，遇雨皆躡釘靴，聲徹殿陛，侍儀司請禁之。

translations.literal: Earlier, all officials entering court, encountering rain all trod nailed boots, sound penetrating hall steps, Ceremonial Service requested prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when officials entered court in rain they all wore nailed boots, whose sound echoed through the hall; the Ceremonial Service asked that this be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「古者入朝有履，自唐始用靴。

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "In antiquity entering court had shoes, from Tang began using boots.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu said, "In antiquity officials wore shoes in court; boots began only in Tang.

sentences.zh: 其令朝官為軟底皮鞋，冒於靴外，出朝則釋之。」

translations.literal: Order court officials make soft-soled leather shoes, cover outside boots, leaving court then remove them."
translations.idiomatic: Let court officials wear soft-soled leather shoes over their boots and remove them when leaving court."

sentences.zh: 禮部言近奢侈越制。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said recently luxury exceeded regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites reported that luxury and violations of rank had lately increased.

sentences.zh: 詔申禁之，仍參酌漢、唐之制，頒行遵守。

translations.literal: An edict reiterated prohibition, still consulting Han Tang systems, promulgated for observance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reiterated the ban and, drawing on Han and Tang regulations, promulgated rules for all to follow.

sentences.zh: 凡職官，一品、二品用雜色文綺、綾羅、彩繡，帽頂、帽珠用玉；

translations.literal: All ranked officials, first second rank used mixed-color patterned silk, gauze silk, colored embroidery, cap top cap bead used jade;
translations.idiomatic: Ranked officials: first and second ranks used patterned silks, gauze silks, and colored embroidery, with jade cap-tops and cap-beads;

sentences.zh: 三品至五品用雜色文綺、綾羅，帽頂用金，帽珠除玉外，隨所用；

translations.literal: Third to fifth rank used mixed-color patterned silk gauze silk, cap top used gold, cap bead besides jade, according to what was used;
translations.idiomatic: third through fifth ranks used patterned silks and gauze silks, with gold cap-tops and cap-beads of whatever material was used besides jade;

sentences.zh: 六品至九品用雜色文綺、綾羅，帽頂用銀，帽珠瑪瑙、水晶、香木。

translations.literal: Sixth to ninth rank used mixed-color patterned silk gauze silk, cap top used silver, cap bead agate crystal fragrant wood.
translations.idiomatic: sixth through ninth ranks used patterned silks and gauze silks, with silver cap-tops and cap-beads of agate, crystal, or fragrant wood.

sentences.zh: 一品至六品穿四爪龍，以金繡為之者聽。

translations.literal: First to sixth rank wore four-claw dragons, those using gold embroidery permitted.
translations.idiomatic: First through sixth ranks might wear four-clawed dragons; gold embroidery was permitted.

sentences.zh: 禮部又議：「品官見尊長，用朝君公服，於理未安。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites again discussed: "Ranked officials seeing elders, using court-lord service dress, in principle not proper.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites further argued, "It is improper in principle for ranked officials to greet their elders in the service dress worn when attending the ruler.

sentences.zh: 宜別制樑冠、絳衣、絳裳、革帶、大帶、大白襪、烏舄、佩綬，其衣裳去緣襈。

translations.literal: Should separately make beam-cap, deep-red upper robe, deep-red skirt, leather belt, great sash, great white socks, black shoes, wear tassel sash, their robes remove border pleats.
translations.idiomatic: A separate set should be made: beam-cap, deep-red upper robe and skirt, leather belt, great sash, great white socks, black shoes, and tassel sash, with border pleats removed from the garments.

sentences.zh: 三品以上佩綬，三品以下不用。

translations.literal: Third rank and above wear tassel sash, third rank and below not use.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above wore the tassel sash; below third rank did not.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，令文武官遇雨戴雨帽，公差出外戴帽子，入城不許。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year, ordered civil and military officials encountering rain wear rain hats, on public errand outside wear hats, entering city not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year officials were ordered to wear rain hats in rain and hats on public errands outside the capital, but not to wear hats when entering the city.

sentences.zh: 二十三年定制，文官衣自領至裔，去地一寸，袖長過手，復回至肘。

translations.literal: Twenty-third year fixed system, civil officials' robes from collar to hem, one inch from ground, sleeves length past hands, return again to elbow.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the cut was fixed: civil officials' robes from collar to hem stood one inch above the ground, with sleeves past the hands and turned back to the elbow.

sentences.zh: 公、侯、駙馬與文官同。

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law same as civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, marquises, and imperial sons-in-law followed civil officials.

sentences.zh: 武官去地五寸，袖長過手七寸。

translations.literal: Military officials five inches from ground, sleeves length past hands seven inches.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials' robes stood five inches above the ground, with sleeves seven inches past the hands.

sentences.zh: 二十四年定，公、侯、駙馬、伯服，繡麒麟、白澤。

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth year fixed, dukes marquises imperial sons-in-law earls dress, embroidered qilin, white ze.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year it was fixed that dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, and earls wore robes embroidered with qilin and white ze.

sentences.zh: 文官一品仙鶴，二品錦雞，三品孔雀，四品雲雁，五品白鷳，六品鷺鷥，七品鸂氵鶒，八品黃鸝，九品鵪鶉；

translations.literal: Civil officials first rank immortal crane, second rank golden pheasant, third rank peacock, fourth rank cloud goose, fifth rank white egret, sixth rank egret, seventh rank xichi, eighth rank yellow oriole, ninth rank quail;
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials: first rank, immortal crane; second rank, golden pheasant; third rank, peacock; fourth rank, cloud goose; fifth rank, white egret; sixth rank, egret; seventh rank, xichi; eighth rank, yellow oriole; ninth rank, quail;

sentences.zh: 雜職練鵲；

translations.literal: Miscellaneous posts practice magpie;
translations.idiomatic: miscellaneous posts, practice magpie;

sentences.zh: 風憲官獬廌。

translations.literal: Censorial officials xiezhi.
translations.idiomatic: censorial officials, xiezhi.

sentences.zh: 武官一品、二品獅子，三品、四品虎豹，五品熊羆，六品、七品彪，八品犀牛，九品海馬。

translations.literal: Military officials first second rank lion, third fourth rank tiger leopard, fifth rank bear, sixth seventh rank leopard-cat, eighth rank rhinoceros, ninth rank sea horse.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials: first and second ranks, lion; third and fourth ranks, tiger and leopard; fifth rank, bear; sixth and seventh ranks, leopard-cat; eighth rank, rhinoceros; ninth rank, sea horse.

sentences.zh: 又令品官常服用雜色紵絲、綾羅、彩繡。

translations.literal: Again ordered ranked officials' regular dress use mixed-color ramie silk, gauze silk, colored embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked officials were again ordered to use mixed-color ramie silk, gauze silk, and colored embroidery for regular dress.

sentences.zh: 官吏衣服、帳幔，不許用玄、黃、紫三色，並織繡龍鳳文，違者罪及染造之人。

translations.literal: Officials' clothes, curtains, not permitted to use black, yellow, purple three colors, and weave embroider dragon phoenix patterns, violators guilt extended to dyers makers.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' garments and curtains might not use black, yellow, or purple, nor woven dragon-and-phoenix designs; violators were punished together with those who dyed or wove the cloth.

sentences.zh: 朝見人員，四時並用色衣，不許純素。

translations.literal: Persons attending court, four seasons all used colored robes, not permitted pure plain.
translations.idiomatic: Those attending court wore colored robes in all four seasons and might not wear plain white.

sentences.zh: 三十年，令致仕官服色與見任同，若朝賀、謝恩、見辭，一體具服。

translations.literal: Thirtieth year, ordered retired officials dress colors same as incumbent, if court congratulations thanking grace farewell audience, all fully equipped dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year retired officials were ordered to use the same colors as incumbents; for court congratulations, thanksgiving, and farewell audiences they wore full dress.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年，令錦衣衛指揮侍衛者，得衣麒麟。

translations.literal: Jingtai 4, ordered Brocade Guard commanders on guard attendance, permitted to wear qilin.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 4 Brocade Guard commanders on guard duty were permitted to wear qilin robes.

sentences.zh: 天順二年，定官民衣服不得用蟒龍、飛魚、斗牛、大鵬、像生獅子、四寶相花、大西番蓮、大雲花樣，並玄、黃、紫及玄色、黑、綠、柳黃、薑黃、明黃諸色。

translations.literal: Tianshun 2, fixed officials and commoners' clothes not permitted to use python dragon, flying fish, fighting bull, great peng, lifelike lion, four-treasure facing flowers, great western lotus, great cloud patterns, and black, yellow, purple and black color, green, willow yellow, ginger yellow, bright yellow various colors.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 2 it was fixed that officials and commoners might not use python dragons, flying fish, fighting bulls, great peng birds, lifelike lions, four-treasure facing flowers, great western lotus, great cloud patterns, or the colors black, yellow, purple, plain black, green, willow yellow, ginger yellow, and bright yellow.

sentences.zh: 弘治十三年奏定，公、侯、伯、文武大臣及鎮守、守備，違例奏請蟒衣、飛魚衣服者，科道糾劾，治以重罪。

translations.literal: Hongzhi 13 memorialized and fixed, dukes marquises earls civil military great ministers and garrison commanders, violators memorializing requesting python robes flying fish clothes, censorial officials impeached, punished with heavy crime.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 13 it was memorialized and fixed that dukes, marquises, earls, civil and military ministers, and garrison commanders who improperly petitioned for python or flying-fish robes would be impeached by the censorate and punished severely.

sentences.zh: 正德十一年設東、西兩官廳，將士悉衣黃罩甲。

translations.literal: Zhengde 11 established east west two guard halls, officers and soldiers all wore yellow surcoats.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 11 the eastern and western guard halls were established, and officers and soldiers all wore yellow surcoats.

sentences.zh: 中外化之。

translations.literal: Inside and outside transformed by it.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country followed the fashion.

sentences.zh: 金緋盛服者，亦必加此於上。

translations.literal: Those in gold scarlet full dress, also must add this on top.
translations.idiomatic: Even those in full gold and scarlet dress added the surcoat on top.

sentences.zh: 都督江彬等承日紅笠之上，綴以靛染天鵝翎，以為貴飾，貴者飄三英，次者二英。

translations.literal: Regional commander Jiang Bin and others atop sun-red hats, attached with indigo-dyed swan feathers, as noble ornament, nobles fluttered three plumes, next two plumes.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Jiang Bin and others, atop sun-red hats, attached indigo-dyed swan feathers as a mark of honor: the highest rank wore three plumes, the next rank two.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書王瓊得賜一英，冠以下教場，自謂殊遇。

translations.literal: Minister of War Wang Qiong received gift of one plume, from cap down to drill ground, considered himself special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Wang Qiong received the gift of one plume and, from his cap to the drill ground, regarded it as a singular honor.

sentences.zh: 其後巡狩所經，督餉侍郎、巡撫都御史無不衣罩甲見上者。

translations.literal: Afterward wherever the imperial tour passed, grain-supply vice ministers, grand coordinators all without exception wore surcoats to see the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, wherever the imperial tour passed, grain-supply vice ministers and grand coordinators all wore surcoats when appearing before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 十三年，車駕還京，傳旨，俾迎候者用曳撒大帽、鸞帶。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, imperial carriage returned capital, transmitted order, made those welcoming use trailing-sash great hat, luan belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when the imperial carriage returned to the capital, an order was transmitted that those welcoming it should wear trailing-sash robes, great hats, and luan belts.

sentences.zh: 尋賜羣臣大紅紵絲羅紗各一。

translations.literal: Soon bestowed all ministers great red ramie silk gauze silk each one.
translations.idiomatic: Soon each minister was bestowed a robe of great red ramie silk or gauze.

sentences.zh: 其服色，一品斗牛，二品飛魚，三品蟒，四、五品麒麟，六、七品虎、彪；

translations.literal: Their dress colors, first rank fighting bull, second rank flying fish, third rank python, fourth fifth rank qilin, sixth seventh rank tiger leopard-cat;
translations.idiomatic: The colors were: first rank, fighting bull; second rank, flying fish; third rank, python; fourth and fifth ranks, qilin; sixth and seventh ranks, tiger and leopard-cat;

sentences.zh: 翰林科道不限品級皆與焉；

translations.literal: Hanlin censorial posts without limit on rank all participated;
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin and censorial officials of every rank were included;

sentences.zh: 惟部曹五品下不與。

translations.literal: Only ministry clerks fifth rank and below not included.
translations.idiomatic: only ministry clerks below fifth rank were excluded.

sentences.zh: 時文臣服色亦以走獸，而麒麟之服逮於四品，尤異事也。

translations.literal: At the time civil officials' dress colors also used running beasts, yet qilin dress reached fourth rank, especially strange affair.
translations.idiomatic: At the time civil officials also wore running-beast designs, and qilin robes even reached fourth rank—an especially irregular state of affairs.

sentences.zh: 十六年，世宗登極詔云：「近來冒濫玉帶，蟒龍、飛魚、斗牛服色，皆庶官雜流並各處將領夤緣奏乞，今俱不許。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, Shizong ascended throne edict said: "Recently usurping jade belts, python dragon, flying fish, fighting bull dress colors, all miscellaneous low officials and various place generals by connections memorialized begging, now all not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, on his accession the Shizong issued an edict: "Lately jade belts, python dragons, flying fish, and fighting-bull colors have been usurped through petitions by miscellaneous low officials and regional generals seeking favor by connection; all are now forbidden.

sentences.zh: 武職卑官僭用公、侯服色者，亦禁絕之。

translations.literal: Military low officials usurping duke marquis dress colors, also forbidden and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers of low rank who usurped ducal and marquis colors were likewise forbidden."

sentences.zh: 」嘉靖六年復禁中外官，不許濫服五彩裝花織造違禁顏色。

translations.literal: " Jiajing 6 again forbade inside outside officials, not permitted to usurp wear five-color decorated flower woven forbidden colors.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 6 officials throughout the realm were again forbidden to wear five-colored brocades or forbidden colors.

sentences.zh: 七年既定燕居法服之制，閣臣張璁因言：「品官燕居之服未有明制，詭異之徒，競為奇服以亂典章。

translations.literal: Seventh year already fixed at-home law dress system, Grand Secretary Zhang Cong therefore said: "Ranked officials' at-home dress has no clear system, bizarre persons compete making strange clothes to disorder regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after the regulations for at-home dress were fixed, Grand Secretary Zhang Cong said, "Ranked officials have no clear regulations for at-home dress, and eccentric persons compete in strange garments that disorder the statutes.

sentences.zh: 乞更法古玄端，別為簡易之制，昭布天下，使貴賤有等。

translations.literal: Beg to reform following ancient dark robe, separately make simple system, proclaim throughout realm, make noble and base have gradations.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that we follow the ancient dark robe in devising a simpler system, proclaim it throughout the realm, and restore proper gradations between high and low."

sentences.zh: 」帝因復製《忠靜冠服圖》頒禮部，敕諭之曰：「祖宗稽古定制，品官朝祭之服，各有等差。

translations.literal: " The emperor therefore again made "Loyal Tranquility Cap and Dress Illustrations" issued to Ministry of Rites, imperial order instructed saying: "Ancestors consulted antiquity fixed systems, ranked officials' court sacrifice dress, each had gradations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore drew up Illustrations of the Loyal Tranquility Cap and Dress and issued them to the Ministry of Rites, instructing: "Our ancestors consulted antiquity and fixed systems by which ranked officials' court and sacrificial dress each had its gradation.

sentences.zh: 第常人之情，多謹於明顯，怠於幽獨。

translations.literal: Only ordinary persons' feelings, mostly careful in the obvious, negligent in secluded solitude.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ordinary human nature is careful in public and negligent in private.

sentences.zh: 古聖王慎之，制玄端以為燕居之服。

translations.literal: Ancient sage kings were cautious of this, made dark robe as at-home dress.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sage kings were mindful of this and made the dark robe for at-home dress.

sentences.zh: 比來衣服詭異，上下無辨，民志何由定。

translations.literal: Recently clothes bizarre, above below without distinction, people's will how can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lately clothing has grown bizarre, high and low are indistinguishable, and the people's standards cannot be settled.

sentences.zh: 朕因酌古玄端之制，更名『忠靜』，庶幾乎進思盡忠，退思補過焉。

translations.literal: I therefore drew on ancient dark robe system, renamed "Loyal Tranquility," hoping perhaps advancing think exhaust loyalty, retiring think remedy faults.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore drawn on the ancient dark robe and renamed it Loyal Tranquility, so that in advancing one may think of loyalty and in retiring one may think of correcting faults.

sentences.zh: 朕已著為圖說，如式製造。

translations.literal: I have already composed illustrations and explanations, according to pattern manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: I have already drawn up illustrations and explanations; make the garments according to the pattern.

sentences.zh: 在京許七品以上官及八品以上翰林院、國子監、行人司，在外許方面官及各府堂官、州縣正堂、儒學教官服之。

translations.literal: In capital permitted seventh rank and above officials and eighth rank and above Hanlin Academy, Directorate of Education, Foreign Envoys Office, outside permitted regional officials and each prefecture hall officials, district county chief seats, Confucian school instructors to wear it.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, officials of seventh rank and above, and in the Hanlin Academy, Directorate of Education, and Foreign Envoys Office of eighth rank and above, may wear it; outside the capital, regional officials, prefectural hall officers, district and county chief magistrates, and Confucian instructors may wear it.

sentences.zh: 武官止都督以上。

translations.literal: Military officials only regional commanders and above.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers are limited to regional commanders and above.

sentences.zh: 其餘不許濫服。

translations.literal: The rest not permitted to usurp wear.
translations.idiomatic: All others are forbidden to wear it improperly.

sentences.zh: 」禮部以圖說頒佈天下，如敕奉行。

translations.literal: " Ministry of Rites with illustrations and explanations proclaimed throughout realm, as ordered observed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites proclaimed the illustrations throughout the realm, and all obeyed as ordered.

sentences.zh: 按忠靜冠仿古玄冠，冠匡如制，以烏紗冒之，兩山俱列於後。

translations.literal: According to Loyal Tranquility cap imitating ancient dark cap, cap frame as regulations, covered with black gauze, two mountains all arranged at rear.
translations.idiomatic: The Loyal Tranquility cap imitated the ancient dark cap: the frame followed regulation, was covered with black gauze, and both mountain-flanges were set at the rear.

sentences.zh: 冠頂仍方中微起，三樑各壓以金線，邊以金緣之。

translations.literal: Cap top still square center slightly raised, three ridges each pressed with gold thread, border with gold edged.
translations.idiomatic: The crown top remained slightly raised at the square center; three ridges were each bound with gold thread and the border was edged in gold.

sentences.zh: 四品以下，去金，緣以淺色絲線。

translations.literal: Fourth rank and below, removed gold, edged with light-color silk thread.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank and below omitted gold and used light-colored silk edging.

sentences.zh: 忠靜服仿古玄端服，色用深青，以紵絲紗羅為之。

translations.literal: Loyal Tranquility dress imitating ancient dark robe dress, color used deep blue-green, made with ramie silk gauze silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Loyal Tranquility robe imitated the ancient dark robe, in deep blue-green ramie silk, gauze, or silk.

sentences.zh: 三品以上雲，四品以下素，緣以藍青，前後飾本等花樣補子。

translations.literal: Third rank and above clouds, fourth rank and below plain, bordered with blue-green, front rear decorated with their rank pattern badges.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above bore cloud patterns; fourth rank and below were plain; all were bordered in blue-green and bore rank badges front and rear.

sentences.zh: 深衣用玉色。

translations.literal: Deep robe used jade color.
translations.idiomatic: The deep robe was jade-colored.

sentences.zh: 素帶，如古大夫之帶制，青表綠緣邊並裏。

translations.literal: Plain sash, like ancient great officers' sash system, blue-green surface green border edge and lining.
translations.idiomatic: The plain sash followed the ancient great officer's sash: blue-green on the surface, green border and lining.

sentences.zh: 素履，青綠絛結。

translations.literal: Plain shoes, blue-green cord knots.
translations.idiomatic: Plain shoes with blue-green cord ties.

sentences.zh: 白襪。

translations.literal: White socks.
translations.idiomatic: White socks.

sentences.zh: 十六年，羣臣朝於駐蹕所，兵部尚書張瓚服蟒。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, ministers attended court at temporary residence, Minister of War Zhang Zan wore python.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when ministers attended court at the temporary residence, Minister of War Zhang Zan wore a python robe.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，諭閣臣夏言曰：「尚書二品，何自服蟒？

translations.literal: Emperor angry, instructed Grand Secretary Xia Yan saying: "Minister second rank, why himself wear python?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and told Grand Secretary Xia Yan, "A minister of second rank—why is he wearing python?

sentences.zh: 」言對曰：「瓚所服，乃欽賜飛魚服，鮮明類蟒耳。

translations.literal: " Yan replied saying: "What Zan wears is imperially bestowed flying fish dress, bright resembling python only.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "What Zhang wears is an imperially bestowed flying-fish robe; it is bright and merely resembles python.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「飛魚何組兩角？

translations.literal: " Emperor said: "Flying fish how woven two horns?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How does a flying fish have two horns woven into it?

sentences.zh: 其嚴禁之。

translations.literal: Strictly forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Forbid it strictly."

sentences.zh: 」於是禮部奏定，文武官不許擅用蟒衣、飛魚、斗牛、違禁華異服色。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Ministry of Rites memorialized and fixed, civil military officials not permitted to usurp use python robes, flying fish, fighting bull, forbidden splendid strange dress colors.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites then memorialized and fixed that civil and military officials might not usurp python robes, flying fish, fighting bulls, or other forbidden splendid colors.

sentences.zh: 其大紅紵絲紗羅服，惟四品以上官及在京五品堂上官、經筵講官許服。

translations.literal: Their great red ramie silk gauze silk dress, only fourth rank and above officials and in capital fifth rank hall officials, Classics Lectern lecturers permitted to wear.
translations.idiomatic: Great red ramie, gauze, or silk robes were permitted only to officials of fourth rank and above, to fifth-rank hall officers in the capital, and to Classics Lectern lecturers.

sentences.zh: 五品官及經筵不為講官者，俱服青綠錦繡。

translations.literal: Fifth rank officials and Classics Lectern not lecturers, all wore blue-green brocade embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-rank officials and those at the Classics Lectern who were not lecturers all wore blue-green brocade.

sentences.zh: 遇吉禮，止衣紅布絨褐。

translations.literal: Encountering auspicious rites, only wore red cloth fleece brown.
translations.idiomatic: For auspicious rites they wore only red cloth or fleece-brown garments.

sentences.zh: 品官花樣，並依品級。

translations.literal: Ranked officials' patterns, all according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked officials' patterns all followed rank.

sentences.zh: 錦衣衛指揮，侍衛者仍得衣麒麟，其帶俸非侍衛，及千百戶雖侍衛，不許僭用。

translations.literal: Brocade Guard commanders, on guard attendance still permitted to wear qilin, those with salary not on guard, and centurion sub-officers though on guard, not permitted to usurp use.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade Guard commanders on guard duty might still wear qilin; those on salary but not on guard, and centurions and sub-officers even if on guard, might not usurp the privilege.

sentences.zh: 歷朝賜服：文臣有未至一品而賜玉帶者，自洪武中學士羅復仁始。

translations.literal: Successive dynasties bestowed dress: civil ministers not yet reaching first rank yet bestowed jade belt, from Hongwu Academician Luo Furen began.
translations.idiomatic: Imperially bestowed dress through the ages: civil ministers below first rank who received jade belts began with Academician Luo Furen in Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 衍聖公秩正二品，服織金麒麟袍、玉帶，則景泰中入朝拜賜。

translations.literal: Duke of Yansheng rank orthodox second rank, wore woven gold qilin robe jade belt, then in Jingtai entering court bowing bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Yansheng, though of orthodox second rank, received woven-gold qilin robes and jade belts when he entered court to bow in Jingtai.

sentences.zh: 自是以為常。

translations.literal: From this became regular.
translations.idiomatic: This thereafter became customary.

sentences.zh: 內閣賜蟒衣，自弘治中劉健、李東陽始。

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat bestowed python robes, from Hongzhi Liu Jian, Li Dongyang began.
translations.idiomatic: Python robes bestowed on the Grand Secretariat began with Liu Jian and Li Dongyang in Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 麒麟本公、侯服，而內閣服之，則嘉靖中嚴嵩、徐階皆受賜也。

translations.literal: Qilin originally duke marquis dress, yet Grand Secretariat wore it, then in Jiajing Yan Song, Xu Jie all received bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Qilin was originally ducal and marquis dress, yet the Grand Secretariat wore it; in Jiajing both Yan Song and Xu Jie received the gift.

sentences.zh: 仙鶴，文臣一品服也，嘉靖中成國公硃希忠、都督陸炳服之，皆以玄壇供事。

translations.literal: Immortal crane, civil minister first rank dress, in Jiajing Duke of Chengguo Zhu Xizhong, regional commander Lu Bing wore it, all because of Mysterious Altar service.
translations.idiomatic: The immortal crane was first-rank civil dress; in Jiajing the Duke of Chengguo Zhu Xizhong and regional commander Lu Bing wore it because they served at the Mysterious Altar.

sentences.zh: 而學士嚴訥、李春芳、董份以五品撰青詞，亦賜仙鶴。

translations.literal: Yet academicians Yan Ne, Li Chunfang, Dong Fen as fifth rank composing green lyrics, also bestowed immortal crane.
translations.idiomatic: Yet academicians Yan Ne, Li Chunfang, and Dong Fen, though only fifth rank and composing green lyrics, were also bestowed the immortal crane.

sentences.zh: 尋諭供事壇中乃用，於是尚書皆不敢衣鶴。

translations.literal: Soon instructed only those serving at altar might use, thereupon ministers all dared not wear crane.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it was ordered that only those serving at the altar might wear it, and thereafter ministers dared not wear the crane.

sentences.zh: 後敕南京織閃黃補麒麟、仙鶴，賜嚴嵩，閃黃乃上用服色也；

translations.literal: Later ordered Nanjing weave flashing yellow patch qilin immortal crane, bestowed Yan Song, flashing yellow was emperor's upper-use color;
translations.idiomatic: Later Nanjing was ordered to weave flashing-yellow patches with qilin and immortal crane and bestow them on Yan Song—flashing yellow being an emperor's color;

sentences.zh: 又賜徐階教子昇天蟒。

translations.literal: Again bestowed Xu Jie teaching son ascending heaven python.
translations.idiomatic: and Xu Jie was also bestowed a python robe showing a son teaching his father to ascend to heaven.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，賜張居正坐蟒；

translations.literal: In Wanli, bestowed Zhang Juzheng seated python;
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli, Zhang Juzheng was bestowed a seated-python robe;

sentences.zh: 武清侯李偉以太后父，亦受賜。

translations.literal: Marquis of Wuqing Li Wei as empress dowager's father, also received bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: and Marquis of Wuqing Li Wei, as the empress dowager's father, also received the gift.

sentences.zh: 儀賓朝服、公服、常服：俱視品級，與文武官同，惟笏皆象牙；

translations.literal: Ceremonial sons-in-law court dress, service dress, regular dress: all according to rank, same as civil military officials, only tablets all ivory;
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial sons-in-law's court, service, and regular dress all followed rank like civil and military officials, but all court tablets were ivory;

sentences.zh: 常服花樣視武官。

translations.literal: Regular dress patterns viewed as military officials.
translations.idiomatic: regular-dress patterns followed military officials.

sentences.zh: 弘治十三年定，郡主儀賓鈒花金帶，胸背獅子。

translations.literal: Hongzhi 13 fixed, commandery princess ceremonial son-in-law chased flower gold belt, chest back lion.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed in Hongzhi 13: a commandery princess's ceremonial son-in-law wore a chased-flower gold belt and lion badges on chest and back.

sentences.zh: 縣主儀賓鈒花金帶，郡君儀賓光素金帶，胸背俱虎豹。

translations.literal: County princess ceremonial son-in-law chased flower gold belt, commandery lady ceremonial son-in-law plain bright gold belt, chest back all tiger leopard.
translations.idiomatic: A county princess's son-in-law wore a chased-flower gold belt; a commandery lady's son-in-law wore plain bright gold; both bore tiger-and-leopard badges.

sentences.zh: 縣君儀賓鈒花銀帶，鄉君儀賓光素銀帶，胸背俱彪。

translations.literal: County lady ceremonial son-in-law chased flower silver belt, township lady ceremonial son-in-law plain bright silver belt, chest back all leopard-cat.
translations.idiomatic: A county lady's son-in-law wore chased-flower silver; a township lady's son-in-law wore plain bright silver; both bore leopard-cat badges.

sentences.zh: 有僭用者，革去冠帶，戴平頭巾，於儒學讀書習禮三年。

translations.literal: Those usurping use, stripped of cap belt, wore plain headcloth, at Confucian school read books study rites three years.
translations.idiomatic: Usurpers were stripped of cap and belt, made to wear a plain headcloth, and sent to a Confucian school to study rites for three years.

sentences.zh: 狀元及諸進士冠服：狀元冠二樑，緋羅圓領，白絹中單，錦綬，蔽膝，紗帽，槐木笏，光銀帶，藥玉佩，朝靴，氈襪，皆御前頒賜，上表謝恩日服之。

translations.literal: Top graduate and all presented scholars caps and robes: top graduate cap two ridges, scarlet gauze round collar, white silk under-robe, brocade sash, knee-apron, gauze cap, locust wood tablet, bright silver belt, medicinal jade pendant, court boots, felt socks, all imperial presence bestowed, on memorial thanking grace day wore them.
translations.idiomatic: Caps and dress of the top graduate and presented scholars: the top graduate wore a two-ridged cap, scarlet gauze round-collared robe, white silk under-robe, brocade sash, knee-apron, gauze cap, locust-wood tablet, bright silver belt, medicinal-jade pendant, court boots, and felt socks—all bestowed before the throne and worn on the day of the thanksgiving memorial.

sentences.zh: 進士巾如烏紗帽，頂微平，展角闊寸餘，長五寸許，系以垂帶，皁紗為之。

translations.literal: Presented scholars' cap like black gauze cap, top slightly flat, spread corners wide over one inch, length about five inches, tied with hanging ribbons, black gauze made it.
translations.idiomatic: Presented scholars' caps resembled the black gauze cap, with a slightly flat top, spread corners a little over an inch wide and about five inches long, tied with hanging ribbons of black gauze.

sentences.zh: 深藍羅袍，緣以青羅，袖廣而不殺。

translations.literal: Deep blue gauze robe, bordered with blue gauze, sleeves wide without tapering.
translations.idiomatic: A deep blue gauze robe bordered in blue gauze, with wide untapered sleeves.

sentences.zh: 槐木笏，革帶、青鞓，飾以黑角，垂撻尾於後。

translations.literal: Locust wood tablet, leather belt blue girdle, decorated with black horn, hung tassel tails behind.
translations.idiomatic: A locust-wood tablet, leather belt with blue girdle decorated in black horn, with tassel tails hanging behind.

sentences.zh: 廷試後頒於國子監，傳臚日服之。

translations.literal: After palace examination bestowed at Directorate of Education, transmission of felicitations day wore them.
translations.idiomatic: After the palace examination they were issued at the Directorate of Education and worn on the day of the transmission of felicitations.

sentences.zh: 上表謝恩後，謁先師行釋菜禮畢，始易常服，其巾袍仍送國子監藏之。

translations.literal: After memorial thanking grace, visiting former teacher performing vegetable-release rite completed, then changed to regular dress, their cap robes still sent to Directorate of Education stored.
translations.idiomatic: After the thanksgiving memorial, and after visiting the former teacher and performing the vegetable-release rite, they changed to regular dress; the cap and robe were sent back to the Directorate of Education for storage.

sentences.zh: 命婦冠服：洪武元年定，命婦一品，冠花釵九樹。

translations.literal: Titled ladies' caps and robes: Fixed Hongwu 1, titled lady first rank, cap flower hairpins nine trees.
translations.idiomatic: On titled ladies' caps and dress: Fixed in Hongwu 1, a first-rank titled lady's cap bore flower hairpins of nine trees.

sentences.zh: 兩博鬢，九鈿。

translations.literal: Two broad side-locks, nine tin ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Two broad side-locks and nine tin ornaments.

sentences.zh: 服用翟衣，繡翟九重。

translations.literal: Wore pheasant robe, embroidered pheasant nine layers.
translations.idiomatic: She wore a pheasant robe embroidered with nine layers of pheasant.

sentences.zh: 素紗中單，黼領，硃縠逯襈裾。

translations.literal: Plain gauze under-robe, fu-pattern collar, vermilion grain continuous-border skirt.
translations.idiomatic: A plain gauze under-robe with fu-pattern collar and vermilion continuous-border skirt.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝隨裳色，以緅為領緣，加文繡重翟，為章二等。

translations.literal: Knee-apron followed skirt color, with dark red as collar border, added patterned embroidery layered pheasant, as insignia two grades.
translations.idiomatic: The knee-apron matched the skirt, with dark-red collar border, layered embroidered pheasant as insignia of two grades.

sentences.zh: 玉帶。

translations.literal: Jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: A jade belt.

sentences.zh: 青襪舄，佩綬。

translations.literal: Blue socks shoes, wore tassel sash.
translations.idiomatic: Blue socks and shoes, with tassel sash.

sentences.zh: 二品，冠花釵八樹。

translations.literal: Second rank, cap flower hairpins eight trees.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank: flower hairpins of eight trees.

sentences.zh: 兩博鬢，八鈿。

translations.literal: Two broad side-locks, eight tin ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Two broad side-locks and eight tin ornaments.

sentences.zh: 服用翟衣八等，犀帶，餘如一品。

translations.literal: Wore pheasant robe eight grades, rhinoceros belt, remainder same as first rank.
translations.idiomatic: A pheasant robe of eight grades, rhinoceros-horn belt; otherwise the same as first rank.

sentences.zh: 三品，冠花釵七樹。

translations.literal: Third rank, cap flower hairpins seven trees.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank: flower hairpins of seven trees.

sentences.zh: 兩博鬢，七鈿。

translations.literal: Two broad side-locks, seven tin ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Two broad side-locks and seven tin ornaments.

sentences.zh: 翟衣七等，金革帶，餘如二品。

translations.literal: Pheasant robe seven grades, gold leather belt, remainder same as second rank.
translations.idiomatic: A pheasant robe of seven grades, gold leather belt; otherwise the same as second rank.

sentences.zh: 四品，冠花釵六樹。

translations.literal: Fourth rank, cap flower hairpins six trees.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank: flower hairpins of six trees.

sentences.zh: 兩博鬢，六鈿。

translations.literal: Two broad side-locks, six tin ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Two broad side-locks and six tin ornaments.

sentences.zh: 翟衣六等，金革帶，餘如三品。

translations.literal: Pheasant robe six grades, gold leather belt, remainder same as third rank.
translations.idiomatic: A pheasant robe of six grades, gold leather belt; otherwise the same as third rank.

sentences.zh: 五品，冠花釵五樹。

translations.literal: Fifth rank, cap flower hairpins five trees.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: flower hairpins of five trees.

sentences.zh: 兩博鬢，五鈿。

translations.literal: Two broad side-locks, five tin ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Two broad side-locks and five tin ornaments.

sentences.zh: 翟衣五等，烏角帶，餘如四品。

translations.literal: Pheasant robe five grades, black horn belt, remainder same as fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: A pheasant robe of five grades, black horn belt; otherwise the same as fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 六品，冠花釵四樹。

translations.literal: Sixth rank, cap flower hairpins four trees.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank: flower hairpins of four trees.

sentences.zh: 兩博鬢，四鈿。

translations.literal: Two broad side-locks, four tin ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Two broad side-locks and four tin ornaments.

sentences.zh: 翟衣四等，烏角帶，餘如五品。

translations.literal: Pheasant robe four grades, black horn belt, remainder same as fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: A pheasant robe of four grades, black horn belt; otherwise the same as fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 七品，冠花釵三樹。

translations.literal: Seventh rank, cap flower hairpins three trees.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh rank: flower hairpins of three trees.

sentences.zh: 兩博鬢，三鈿。

translations.literal: Two broad side-locks, three tin ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Two broad side-locks and three tin ornaments.

sentences.zh: 翟衣三等，烏角帶，餘如六品。

translations.literal: Pheasant robe three grades, black horn belt, remainder same as sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: A pheasant robe of three grades, black horn belt; otherwise the same as sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 自一品至五品，衣色隨夫用紫。

translations.literal: From first to fifth rank, robe color followed the husband in using purple.
translations.idiomatic: From first through fifth rank, robe color followed the husband's and was purple.

sentences.zh: 六品、七品，衣色隨夫用緋。

translations.literal: Sixth and seventh ranks, robe color followed the husband in using scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth and seventh ranks wore scarlet, following their husbands' color.

sentences.zh: 其大帶如衣色。

translations.literal: Their great sash matched the robe color.
translations.idiomatic: The great sash matched the robe color.

sentences.zh: 四年，以古天子諸侯服袞冕，後與夫人亦服禕翟。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, following the ancient Son of Heaven and feudal lords' wearing of dragon-and-phoenix robes and coronets, empresses and ladies also wore Yi-style pheasant robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, following the ancient custom by which the Son of Heaven and feudal lords wore dragon-and-phoenix robes and coronets, empresses and their ladies also wore Yi-style pheasant robes.

sentences.zh: 今羣臣既以樑冠、絳衣為朝服，不敢用冕，則外命婦亦不當服翟衣以朝。

translations.literal: Now that officials already take the beam-cap and deep-red robes as court dress and dare not use the coronet, then outer titled ladies also ought not wear pheasant robes to court.
translations.idiomatic: Since officials now wore the beam-cap and deep-red robes as court dress and no longer dared use the coronet, titled ladies outside the inner court likewise ought not wear pheasant robes at court.

sentences.zh: 命禮部議之。

translations.literal: Ordered the Ministry of Rites to deliberate on it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to deliberate the matter.

sentences.zh: 奏定，命婦以山鬆特髻、假鬢花鈿、真紅大袖衣、珠翠蹙金霞帔為朝服。

translations.literal: Memorial fixed it: titled ladies took mountain-pine special topknot, false side-lock flower tin ornaments, true-red large-sleeved robe, pearl-and-kingfisher couched-gold cloud collar as court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Upon memorial it was fixed that titled ladies' court dress would comprise a mountain-pine special topknot, false side-lock flower-and-tin ornaments, a true-red large-sleeved robe, and a pearl-and-kingfisher couched-gold cloud collar.

sentences.zh: 以硃翠角冠、金珠花釵、闊袖雜色綠緣為燕居之用。

translations.literal: Used vermilion kingfisher horn crown, gold pearl flower hairpins, wide-sleeved multicolored green-bordered garments for everyday residence.
translations.idiomatic: For everyday wear they used a vermilion kingfisher horn crown, gold-and-pearl flower hairpins, and wide-sleeved garments of mixed colors with green borders.

sentences.zh: 一品，衣金繡文霞帔，金珠翠妝飾，玉墜。

translations.literal: First rank, wore gold-embroidered patterned cloud collar, gold pearl kingfisher ornaments, jade pendant.
translations.idiomatic: First rank: a cloud collar embroidered in gold with patterned designs, gold pearl-and-kingfisher ornaments, and a jade pendant.

sentences.zh: 二品，衣金繡雲肩大雜花霞帔，金珠翠妝飾，金墜子。

translations.literal: Second rank, wore gold-embroidered cloud-shoulder large mixed-flower cloud collar, gold pearl kingfisher ornaments, gold pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank: a cloud collar with gold-embroidered cloud-shoulder and large mixed floral designs, gold pearl-and-kingfisher ornaments, and a gold pendant.

sentences.zh: 三品，衣金繡大雜花霞帔，珠翠妝飾，金墜子。

translations.literal: Third rank, wore gold-embroidered large mixed-flower cloud collar, pearl kingfisher ornaments, gold pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank: a cloud collar with gold-embroidered large mixed floral designs, pearl-and-kingfisher ornaments, and a gold pendant.

sentences.zh: 四品，衣繡小雜花霞帔，翠妝飾，金墜子。

translations.literal: Fourth rank, wore embroidered small mixed-flower cloud collar, kingfisher ornaments, gold pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank: a cloud collar embroidered with small mixed floral designs, kingfisher ornaments, and a gold pendant.

sentences.zh: 五品，衣銷金大雜花霞帔，生色畫絹起花妝飾，金墜子。

translations.literal: Fifth rank, wore cut-gold large mixed-flower cloud collar, printed colored silk raised-flower ornaments, gold pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: a cut-gold cloud collar with large mixed floral designs, printed colored-silk raised-flower ornaments, and a gold pendant.

sentences.zh: 六品、七品，衣銷金小雜花霞帔，生色畫絹起花妝飾，鍍金銀墜子。

translations.literal: Sixth and seventh ranks, wore cut-gold small mixed-flower cloud collar, printed colored silk raised-flower ornaments, gilded silver pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth and seventh ranks: a cut-gold cloud collar with small mixed floral designs, printed colored-silk raised-flower ornaments, and a gilded silver pendant.

sentences.zh: 八品、九品，衣大紅素羅霞帔，生色畫絹妝飾，銀墜子。

translations.literal: Eighth and ninth ranks, wore great red plain gauze cloud collar, printed colored silk ornaments, silver pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth and ninth ranks: a plain great-red gauze cloud collar, printed colored-silk ornaments, and a silver pendant.

sentences.zh: 首飾，一品、二品，金玉珠翠。

translations.literal: Head ornaments: first and second ranks, gold jade pearl kingfisher.
translations.idiomatic: Head ornaments: first and second ranks used gold, jade, pearl, and kingfisher.

sentences.zh: 三品、四品，金珠翠。

translations.literal: Third and fourth ranks, gold pearl kingfisher.
translations.idiomatic: Third and fourth ranks: gold, pearl, and kingfisher.

sentences.zh: 五品，金翠。

translations.literal: Fifth rank, gold kingfisher.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: gold and kingfisher.

sentences.zh: 六品以下，金鍍銀，間用珠。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below, gold-plated silver, occasionally using pearl.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and below: gold-plated silver, with pearls used sparingly.

sentences.zh: 五年，更定品官命婦冠服：一品，禮服用山鬆特髻，翠鬆五株，金翟八，口銜珠結。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, revised the caps and robes of ranked-official titled ladies: first rank, ceremonial dress used mountain-pine special topknot, kingfisher pine sprays five stems, gold pheasants eight, mouths holding pearl knots.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the caps and dress of titled ladies of ranked officials were revised. First rank: for ceremonial dress, a mountain-pine special topknot with five kingfisher pine sprays and eight gold pheasants, each holding a pearl knot in its beak.

sentences.zh: 正面珠翠翟一，珠翠花四朵，珠翠雲喜花三朵；

translations.literal: Front face: pearl-kingfisher pheasant one, pearl-kingfisher flowers four blossoms, pearl-kingfisher auspicious-cloud flowers three blossoms;
translations.idiomatic: On the front: one pearl-and-kingfisher pheasant, four pearl-and-kingfisher flowers, and three pearl-and-kingfisher auspicious-cloud flowers;

sentences.zh: 後鬢珠梭球一，珠翠飛翟一，珠翠梳四，金雲頭連三釵一，珠簾梳一，金簪二；

translations.literal: Rear side-locks: pearl shuttle ball one, pearl-kingfisher flying pheasant one, pearl-kingfisher combs four, gold cloud-head linked triple hairpin one, pearl-curtain comb one, gold hairpins two;
translations.idiomatic: At the rear: one pearl shuttle ball, one pearl-and-kingfisher flying pheasant, four pearl-and-kingfisher combs, one gold cloud-head linked triple hairpin, one pearl-curtain comb, and two gold hairpins;

sentences.zh: 珠梭環一雙。

translations.literal: Pearl shuttle rings one pair.
translations.idiomatic: One pair of pearl shuttle rings.

sentences.zh: 大袖衫，用真紅色。

translations.literal: Large-sleeved robe, used true red color.
translations.idiomatic: The large-sleeved robe was true red.

sentences.zh: 霞帔、褙子，俱用深青色。

translations.literal: Cloud collar, over-jacket, both used deep blue-green color.
translations.idiomatic: Both the cloud collar and over-jacket were deep blue-green.

sentences.zh: 紵絲綾羅紗隨用。

translations.literal: Ramie silk, damask, gauze, plain gauze as used.
translations.idiomatic: Ramie silk, damask, gauze, or plain gauze might be used as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 霞帔上施蹙金繡雲霞翟文，鈒花金墜子。

translations.literal: Cloud collar bore couched-gold embroidered cloud-mist-pheasant pattern, chased-flower gold pendant.
translations.idiomatic: The cloud collar bore couched-gold embroidery of clouds, mist, and pheasants, with a chased-floral gold pendant.

sentences.zh: 褙子上施金繡雲霞翟文。

translations.literal: Over-jacket bore gold-embroidered cloud-mist-pheasant pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The over-jacket bore gold embroidery of clouds, mist, and pheasants.

sentences.zh: 常服用珠翠慶雲冠，珠翠翟三，金翟一，口銜珠結；

translations.literal: Everyday dress used pearl-kingfisher auspicious-cloud crown, pearl-kingfisher pheasants three, gold pheasant one, mouth holding pearl knot;
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress comprised a pearl-and-kingfisher auspicious-cloud crown with three pearl-and-kingfisher pheasants and one gold pheasant, the latter holding a pearl knot in its beak;

sentences.zh: 鬢邊珠翠花二，小珠翠梳一雙，金雲頭連三釵一，金壓鬢雙頭釵二，金腦梳一，金簪二；

translations.literal: Beside the side-locks: pearl-kingfisher flowers two, small pearl-kingfisher combs one pair, gold cloud-head linked triple hairpin one, gold side-lock-pressing double-head hairpins two, gold temple comb one, gold hairpins two;
translations.idiomatic: Beside the side-locks: two pearl-and-kingfisher flowers, one pair of small pearl-and-kingfisher combs, one gold cloud-head linked triple hairpin, two gold side-lock-pressing double-head hairpins, one gold temple comb, and two gold hairpins;

sentences.zh: 金腳珠翠佛面環一雙；

translations.literal: Gold-foot pearl-kingfisher Buddha-face rings one pair;
translations.idiomatic: One pair of gold-foot pearl-and-kingfisher Buddha-face rings;

sentences.zh: 鐲釧皆用金。

translations.literal: Bracelets and armlets all used gold.
translations.idiomatic: Bracelets and armlets were all of gold.

sentences.zh: 長襖長裙，各色紵絲綾羅紗隨用。

translations.literal: Long jacket, long skirt, various colors of ramie silk damask gauze plain gauze as used.
translations.idiomatic: The long jacket and long skirt might be of various colors in ramie silk, damask, gauze, or plain gauze as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 長襖緣襈，或紫或綠，上施蹙金繡雲霞翟文。

translations.literal: Long jacket bordered hem, either purple or green, bore couched-gold embroidered cloud-mist-pheasant pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The long jacket had a bordered hem in purple or green, with couched-gold embroidery of clouds, mist, and pheasants.

sentences.zh: 看帶，用紅綠紫，上施蹙金繡雲霞翟文。

translations.literal: Ornamental sash, used red green purple, bore couched-gold embroidered cloud-mist-pheasant pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The ornamental sash was red, green, or purple, with couched-gold embroidery of clouds, mist, and pheasants.

sentences.zh: 長裙，橫豎金繡纏枝花文。

translations.literal: Long skirt, horizontal and vertical gold-embroidered entwined-branch flower pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The long skirt bore gold embroidery of entwined floral sprays in horizontal and vertical bands.

sentences.zh: 二品，特髻上金翟七，口銜珠結，餘同一品。

translations.literal: Second rank, special topknot bore gold pheasants seven, mouths holding pearl knots, remainder same as first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank: seven gold pheasants on the special topknot, each holding a pearl knot in its beak; otherwise the same as first rank.

sentences.zh: 常服亦與一品同。

translations.literal: Everyday dress also same as first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress was also the same as first rank.

sentences.zh: 三品，特髻上金孔雀六，口銜珠結。

translations.literal: Third rank, special topknot bore gold peacocks six, mouths holding pearl knots.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank: six gold peacocks on the special topknot, each holding a pearl knot in its beak.

sentences.zh: 正面珠翠孔雀一，後鬢翠孔雀二。

translations.literal: Front face: pearl-kingfisher peacock one; rear side-locks: kingfisher peacocks two.
translations.idiomatic: On the front: one pearl-and-kingfisher peacock; at the rear: two kingfisher peacocks.

sentences.zh: 霞帔上施蹙金雲霞孔雀文，鈒花金墜子。

translations.literal: Cloud collar bore couched-gold cloud-mist-peacock pattern, chased-flower gold pendant.
translations.idiomatic: The cloud collar bore couched-gold clouds, mist, and peacocks, with a chased-floral gold pendant.

sentences.zh: 褙子上施金繡雲霞孔雀文，餘同二品。

translations.literal: Over-jacket bore gold-embroidered cloud-mist-peacock pattern, remainder same as second rank.
translations.idiomatic: The over-jacket bore gold embroidery of clouds, mist, and peacocks; otherwise the same as second rank.

sentences.zh: 常服冠上珠翠孔雀三，金孔雀二，口銜珠結。

translations.literal: Everyday dress crown bore pearl-kingfisher peacocks three, gold peacocks two, mouths holding pearl knots.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress: a crown with three pearl-and-kingfisher peacocks and two gold peacocks, each holding a pearl knot in its beak.

sentences.zh: 長襖緣衤巽。

translations.literal: Long jacket bordered hem.
translations.idiomatic: The long jacket had a bordered hem.

sentences.zh: 看帶，或紫或綠，並繡雲霞孔雀文。

translations.literal: Ornamental sash, either purple or green, both embroidered cloud-mist-peacock pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The ornamental sash was purple or green, embroidered with clouds, mist, and peacocks.

sentences.zh: 長裙，橫豎襴並繡纏枝花文，餘同二品。

translations.literal: Long skirt, horizontal and vertical bar-pattern both embroidered entwined-branch flower pattern, remainder same as second rank.
translations.idiomatic: The long skirt bore bar-pattern bands embroidered with entwined floral sprays; otherwise the same as second rank.

sentences.zh: 四品，特髻上金孔雀五，口銜珠結，餘同三品。

translations.literal: Fourth rank, special topknot bore gold peacocks five, mouths holding pearl knots, remainder same as third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank: five gold peacocks on the special topknot, each holding a pearl knot in its beak; otherwise the same as third rank.

sentences.zh: 常服亦與三品同。

translations.literal: Everyday dress also same as third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress was also the same as third rank.

sentences.zh: 五品，特髻上銀鍍金鴛鴦四，口銜珠結。

translations.literal: Fifth rank, special topknot bore silver-gilded mandarin ducks four, mouths holding pearl knots.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: four gilded silver mandarin ducks on the special topknot, each holding a pearl knot in its beak.

sentences.zh: 正面珠翠鴛鴦一，小珠鋪翠雲喜花三朵；

translations.literal: Front face: pearl-kingfisher mandarin duck one, small pearls spread kingfisher auspicious-cloud flowers three blossoms;
translations.idiomatic: On the front: one pearl-and-kingfisher mandarin duck and three small pearl-and-kingfisher auspicious-cloud flowers;

sentences.zh: 後鬢翠鴛鴦二，銀鍍金雲頭連三釵一，小珠簾梳一，鍍金銀簪二；

translations.literal: Rear side-locks: kingfisher mandarin ducks two, silver-gilded cloud-head linked triple hairpin one, small pearl-curtain comb one, gilded silver hairpins two;
translations.idiomatic: At the rear: two kingfisher mandarin ducks, one gilded silver cloud-head linked triple hairpin, one small pearl-curtain comb, and two gilded silver hairpins;

sentences.zh: 小珠梳環一雙。

translations.literal: Small pearl comb rings one pair.
translations.idiomatic: One pair of small pearl comb rings.

sentences.zh: 霞帔上施繡雲霞鴛鴦文，鍍金銀鈒花墜子。

translations.literal: Cloud collar bore embroidered cloud-mist-mandarin duck pattern, gilded silver chased-flower pendant.
translations.idiomatic: The cloud collar bore embroidery of clouds, mist, and mandarin ducks, with a gilded silver chased-floral pendant.

sentences.zh: 褙子上施雲霞鴛鴦文，餘同四品。

translations.literal: Over-jacket bore cloud-mist-mandarin duck pattern, remainder same as fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The over-jacket bore clouds, mist, and mandarin ducks; otherwise the same as fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 常服冠上小珠翠鴛鴦三，鍍金銀鴛鴦二，挑珠牌。

translations.literal: Everyday dress crown bore small pearl-kingfisher mandarin ducks three, gilded silver mandarin ducks two, pearl plaque pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress: a crown with three small pearl-and-kingfisher mandarin ducks, two gilded silver mandarin ducks, and a pearl plaque pendant.

sentences.zh: 鬢邊小珠翠花二朵，雲頭連三釵一，梳一，壓鬢雙頭釵二，鍍金簪二；

translations.literal: Beside the side-locks: small pearl-kingfisher flowers two blossoms, cloud-head linked triple hairpin one, comb one, side-lock-pressing double-head hairpins two, gilded hairpins two;
translations.idiomatic: Beside the side-locks: two small pearl-and-kingfisher flowers, one cloud-head linked triple hairpin, one comb, two side-lock-pressing double-head hairpins, and two gilded hairpins;

sentences.zh: 銀腳珠翠佛面環一雙。

translations.literal: Silver-foot pearl-kingfisher Buddha-face rings one pair.
translations.idiomatic: One pair of silver-foot pearl-and-kingfisher Buddha-face rings.
