sentences.zh: 鐲釧皆用銀鍍金。

translations.literal: Bracelets and armlets all used silver gilded.
translations.idiomatic: Bracelets and armlets were all of gilded silver.

sentences.zh: 長襖緣襈，繡雲霞鴛鴦文。

translations.literal: Long jacket bordered hem, embroidered cloud-mist-mandarin duck pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The long jacket had a bordered hem embroidered with clouds, mist, and mandarin ducks.

sentences.zh: 長裙，橫豎襴繡纏枝花文，餘同四品。

translations.literal: Long skirt, horizontal and vertical bar-pattern embroidered entwined-branch flower pattern, remainder same as fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The long skirt bore bar-pattern bands embroidered with entwined floral sprays; otherwise the same as fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 六品，特髻上翠鬆三株，銀鍍金練鵲四，口銜珠結。

translations.literal: Sixth rank, special topknot bore kingfisher pine sprays three stems, silver-gilded white magpies four, mouths holding pearl knots.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank: three kingfisher pine sprays and four gilded silver white magpies on the special topknot, each holding a pearl knot in its beak.

sentences.zh: 正面銀鍍金練鵲一，小珠翠花四朵；

translations.literal: Front face: silver-gilded white magpie one, small pearl-kingfisher flowers four blossoms;
translations.idiomatic: On the front: one gilded silver white magpie and four small pearl-and-kingfisher flowers;

sentences.zh: 後鬢翠梭球一，翠練鵲二，翠梳四，銀雲頭連三釵一，珠緣翠簾梳一，銀簪二。

translations.literal: Rear side-locks: kingfisher shuttle ball one, kingfisher white magpies two, kingfisher combs four, silver cloud-head linked triple hairpin one, pearl-edged kingfisher curtain comb one, silver hairpins two.
translations.idiomatic: At the rear: one kingfisher shuttle ball, two kingfisher white magpies, four kingfisher combs, one silver cloud-head linked triple hairpin, one pearl-edged kingfisher curtain comb, and two silver hairpins.

sentences.zh: 大袖衫，綾羅槹絹隨所用。

translations.literal: Large-sleeved robe, damask gauze ramie silk as used.
translations.idiomatic: The large-sleeved robe might be of damask, gauze, or ramie silk as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 霞帔施繡雲霞練鵲文，花銀墜子。

translations.literal: Cloud collar bore embroidered cloud-mist-white magpie pattern, floral silver pendant.
translations.idiomatic: The cloud collar bore embroidery of clouds, mist, and white magpies, with a floral silver pendant.

sentences.zh: 褙子上施雲霞練鵲文，餘同五品。

translations.literal: Over-jacket bore cloud-mist-white magpie pattern, remainder same as fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The over-jacket bore clouds, mist, and white magpies; otherwise the same as fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 常服冠上鍍金銀練鵲三，又鍍金銀練鵲二，挑小珠牌；

translations.literal: Everyday dress crown bore gilded silver white magpies three, also gilded silver white magpies two, small pearl plaque pendant;
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress: a crown with three gilded silver white magpies and two more gilded silver white magpies, with a small pearl plaque pendant;

sentences.zh: 鐲釧皆用銀。

translations.literal: Bracelets and armlets all used silver.
translations.idiomatic: Bracelets and armlets were all of silver.

sentences.zh: 長襖緣襈。

translations.literal: Long jacket bordered hem.
translations.idiomatic: The long jacket had a bordered hem.

sentences.zh: 看帶，或紫或綠，繡雲霞練鵲文。

translations.literal: Ornamental sash, either purple or green, embroidered cloud-mist-white magpie pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The ornamental sash was purple or green, embroidered with clouds, mist, and white magpies.

sentences.zh: 長裙，橫豎襴繡纏枝花文，餘同五品。

translations.literal: Long skirt, horizontal and vertical bar-pattern embroidered entwined-branch flower pattern, remainder same as fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The long skirt bore bar-pattern bands embroidered with entwined floral sprays; otherwise the same as fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 七品，禮服、常服俱同六品。

translations.literal: Seventh rank, ceremonial dress and everyday dress both same as sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh rank: both ceremonial dress and everyday dress were the same as sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 其八品、九品禮服，惟用大袖衫、霞帔、褙子。

translations.literal: Their eighth and ninth rank ceremonial dress, only used large-sleeved robe, cloud collar, over-jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth and ninth ranks: ceremonial dress comprised only the large-sleeved robe, cloud collar, and over-jacket.

sentences.zh: 大衫同七品。

translations.literal: Great robe same as seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: The great robe was the same as seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 霞帔上繡纏枝花，鈒花銀墜子。

translations.literal: Cloud collar embroidered entwined-branch flowers, chased-flower silver pendant.
translations.idiomatic: The cloud collar was embroidered with entwined floral sprays and bore a chased-floral silver pendant.

sentences.zh: 褙子上繡摘枝團花。

translations.literal: Over-jacket embroidered plucked-branch round flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The over-jacket was embroidered with plucked-branch round floral medallions.

sentences.zh: 通用小珠慶雲冠。

translations.literal: Generally used small pearl auspicious-cloud crown.
translations.idiomatic: They generally used the small-pearl auspicious-cloud crown.

sentences.zh: 常服亦用小珠慶雲冠，銀間鍍金銀練鵲三，又銀間鍍金銀練鵲二，挑小珠牌；

translations.literal: Everyday dress also used small pearl auspicious-cloud crown, silver interspersed gilded silver white magpies three, also silver interspersed gilded silver white magpies two, small pearl plaque pendant;
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress also used the small-pearl auspicious-cloud crown, with three partly gilded silver white magpies and two more partly gilded silver white magpies, and a small pearl plaque pendant;

sentences.zh: 銀間鍍金雲頭連三釵一，銀間鍍金壓鬢雙頭釵二，銀間鍍金腦梳一，銀間鍍金簪二。

translations.literal: Silver interspersed gilded cloud-head linked triple hairpin one, silver interspersed gilded side-lock-pressing double-head hairpins two, silver interspersed gilded temple comb one, silver interspersed gilded hairpins two.
translations.idiomatic: One partly gilded silver cloud-head linked triple hairpin, two partly gilded silver side-lock-pressing double-head hairpins, one partly gilded silver temple comb, and two partly gilded silver hairpins.

sentences.zh: 長襖緣襈、看帶並繡纏枝花，餘同七品。

translations.literal: Long jacket bordered hem, ornamental sash both embroidered entwined-branch flowers, remainder same as seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: The long jacket's bordered hem and ornamental sash were both embroidered with entwined floral sprays; otherwise the same as seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 又定命婦團衫之制，以紅羅為之，繡重雉為等第。

translations.literal: Also fixed titled ladies' round-collar robe system, made with red gauze, embroidered layered pheasants as rank grades.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were also fixed for titled ladies' round-collar robes of red gauze, with layered embroidered pheasants denoting rank.

sentences.zh: 一品九等，二品八等，三品七等，四品六等，五品五等，六品四等，七品三等，其餘不用繡雉。

translations.literal: First rank nine grades, second rank eight grades, third rank seven grades, fourth rank six grades, fifth rank five grades, sixth rank four grades, seventh rank three grades, the rest did not use embroidered pheasants.
translations.idiomatic: First rank: nine grades of pheasants; second rank: eight; third rank: seven; fourth rank: six; fifth rank: five; sixth rank: four; seventh rank: three; lower ranks bore no embroidered pheasants.

sentences.zh: 二十四年定制，命婦朝見君後，在家見舅姑並夫及祭祀則服禮服。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year regulations were fixed: titled ladies, after audience with the ruler, at home seeing parents-in-law together with husband and at sacrifices then wore ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year it was fixed that titled ladies wore ceremonial dress after audience with the ruler, when receiving parents-in-law at home together with their husbands, and at sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 公侯伯夫人與一品同。

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, and earls' ladies same as first rank.
translations.idiomatic: The ladies of dukes, marquises, and earls were the same as first rank.

sentences.zh: 大袖衫，真紅色。

translations.literal: Large-sleeved robe, true red color.
translations.idiomatic: The large-sleeved robe was true red.

sentences.zh: 一品至五品，紵絲綾羅；

translations.literal: First to fifth ranks, ramie silk damask gauze;
translations.idiomatic: First through fifth ranks: ramie silk or damask gauze;

sentences.zh: 六品至九品，綾羅槹絹。

translations.literal: Sixth to ninth ranks, damask gauze ramie silk.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth through ninth ranks: damask, gauze, or ramie silk.

sentences.zh: 霞帔、褙子皆深青段。

translations.literal: Cloud collar, over-jacket all deep blue satin.
translations.idiomatic: Both the cloud collar and over-jacket were of deep blue satin.

sentences.zh: 公侯及一品、二品，金繡雲霞翟文；

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises and first and second ranks, gold-embroidered cloud-mist-pheasant pattern;
translations.idiomatic: For dukes, marquises, and first and second ranks: gold embroidery of clouds, mist, and pheasants;

sentences.zh: 三品、四品，金繡雲霞孔雀文；

translations.literal: Third and fourth ranks, gold-embroidered cloud-mist-peacock pattern;
translations.idiomatic: Third and fourth ranks: gold embroidery of clouds, mist, and peacocks;

sentences.zh: 五品，繡雲霞鴛鴦文；

translations.literal: Fifth rank, embroidered cloud-mist-mandarin duck pattern;
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: embroidery of clouds, mist, and mandarin ducks;

sentences.zh: 六品、七品，繡雲霞練鵲文。

translations.literal: Sixth and seventh ranks, embroidered cloud-mist-white magpie pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth and seventh ranks: embroidery of clouds, mist, and white magpies.

sentences.zh: 大袖衫，領闊三寸，兩領直下一尺，間綴紐子三，末綴紐子二，紐在掩紐之下，拜則放之。

translations.literal: Large-sleeved robe, collar width three inches, both collar panels hang straight down one foot, three buttons set at intervals, two buttons at the end; the buttons lie beneath the overlapping collar panel, and when bowing they are released.
translations.idiomatic: The large-sleeved robe had a collar three inches wide; both collar panels hung straight down one foot, with three buttons spaced along them and two at the hem. The buttons sat beneath the overlapping collar flap and were released when bowing.

sentences.zh: 霞帔二條，各繡禽七，隨品級用，前四後三。

translations.literal: Cloud collar two strips, each embroidered birds seven, according to rank used, front four rear three.
translations.idiomatic: Two cloud collars, each embroidered with seven birds according to rank—four in front and three in back.

sentences.zh: 墜子中鈒花禽一，四面雲霞文，禽如霞帔，隨品級用。

translations.literal: Pendant center chased-flower bird one, four sides cloud-mist pattern, birds like cloud collar, according to rank used.
translations.idiomatic: The pendant bore one chased-floral bird at its center and cloud-and-mist patterns on all four sides; the birds matched those on the cloud collar and varied by rank.

sentences.zh: 笏以象牙為之。

translations.literal: Tablet with ivory make it.
translations.idiomatic: The tablet was made of ivory.

sentences.zh: 二十六年定，一品，冠用金事件，珠翟五，珠牡丹開頭二，珠半開三，翠雲二十四片，翠牡丹葉一十八片，翠口圈一副，上帶金寶鈿花八，金翟二，口銜珠結二。

translations.literal: Twenty-sixth year fixed, first rank, crown used gold fittings, pearl pheasants five, pearl peony fully open two, pearl half-open three, kingfisher clouds twenty-four pieces, kingfisher peony leaves eighteen pieces, kingfisher mouth-rim one set, above bore gold jeweled hairpin flowers eight, gold pheasants two, mouth held pearl knots two.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed in the twenty-sixth year: for first rank, the crown used gold fittings, with five pearl pheasants, two fully open pearl peonies, three half-open peonies, twenty-four kingfisher-feather cloud pieces, eighteen kingfisher peony leaves, one set of kingfisher mouth-rim, eight gold jeweled hairpin flowers on top, two gold pheasants, and two pearl knots held in the beak.

sentences.zh: 二品至四品，冠用金事件，珠翟四，珠牡丹開頭二，珠半開四，翠雲二十四片，翠牡丹葉一十八片，翠口圈一副，上帶金寶鈿花八，金翟二，口銜珠結二。

translations.literal: Second rank to fourth rank, crown used gold fittings, pearl pheasants four, pearl peony fully open two, pearl half-open four, kingfisher clouds twenty-four pieces, kingfisher peony leaves eighteen pieces, kingfisher mouth-rim one set, above bore gold jeweled hairpin flowers eight, gold pheasants two, mouth held pearl knots two.
translations.idiomatic: Second through fourth ranks: the crown used gold fittings, with four pearl pheasants, two fully open pearl peonies, four half-open peonies, twenty-four kingfisher cloud pieces, eighteen kingfisher peony leaves, one set of kingfisher mouth-rim, eight gold jeweled hairpin flowers on top, two gold pheasants, and two pearl knots held in the beak.

sentences.zh: 一品、二品，霞帔、褙子俱雲霞翟文，鈒花金墜子。

translations.literal: First and second ranks, cloud collar and over-jacket all cloud-mist-pheasant pattern, chased-flower gold pendant.
translations.idiomatic: First and second ranks: both cloud collar and over-jacket bore clouds, mist, and pheasants, with a chased-floral gold pendant.

sentences.zh: 三品、四品，霞帔、褙子俱雲霞孔雀文，鈒花金墜子。

translations.literal: Third and fourth ranks, cloud collar and over-jacket all cloud-mist-peacock pattern, chased-flower gold pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Third and fourth ranks: both cloud collar and over-jacket bore clouds, mist, and peacocks, with a chased-floral gold pendant.

sentences.zh: 五品、六品，冠用抹金銀事件，珠翟三，珠牡丹開頭二，珠半開五，翠雲二十四片，翠牡丹葉一十八片，翠口圈一副，上帶抹金銀寶鈿花八，抹金銀翟二，口銜珠結子二。

translations.literal: Fifth and sixth ranks, crown used gilt-silver fittings, pearl pheasants three, pearl peony fully open two, pearl half-open five, kingfisher clouds twenty-four pieces, kingfisher peony leaves eighteen pieces, kingfisher mouth-rim one set, above bore gilt-silver jeweled hairpin flowers eight, gilt-silver pheasants two, mouth held pearl knot pendants two.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth and sixth ranks: the crown used gilt-silver fittings, with three pearl pheasants, two fully open pearl peonies, five half-open peonies, twenty-four kingfisher cloud pieces, eighteen kingfisher peony leaves, one set of kingfisher mouth-rim, eight gilt-silver jeweled hairpin flowers on top, two gilt-silver pheasants, and two pearl knot pendants held in the beak.

sentences.zh: 五品，霞帔、褙子俱雲霞鴛鴦文，鍍金鈒花銀墜子。

translations.literal: Fifth rank, cloud collar and over-jacket all cloud-mist-mandarin duck pattern, gold-plated chased-flower silver pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: both cloud collar and over-jacket bore clouds, mist, and mandarin ducks, with a gold-plated chased-floral silver pendant.

sentences.zh: 六品，霞帔、褙子俱雲霞練鵲文，鈒花銀墜子。

translations.literal: Sixth rank, cloud collar and over-jacket all cloud-mist-white magpie pattern, chased-flower silver pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank: both cloud collar and over-jacket bore clouds, mist, and white magpies, with a chased-floral silver pendant.

sentences.zh: 七品至九品，冠用抹金銀事件，珠翟二，珠月桂開頭二，珠半開六，翠雲二十四片，翠月桂葉一十八片，翠口圈一副，上帶抹金銀寶鈿花八，抹金銀翟二，口銜珠結子二。

translations.literal: Seventh rank to ninth rank, crown used gilt-silver fittings, pearl pheasants two, pearl osmanthus fully open two, pearl half-open six, kingfisher clouds twenty-four pieces, kingfisher osmanthus leaves eighteen pieces, kingfisher mouth-rim one set, above bore gilt-silver jeweled hairpin flowers eight, gilt-silver pheasants two, mouth held pearl knot pendants two.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh through ninth ranks: the crown used gilt-silver fittings, with two pearl pheasants, two fully open pearl osmanthus blossoms, six half-open blossoms, twenty-four kingfisher cloud pieces, eighteen kingfisher osmanthus leaves, one set of kingfisher mouth-rim, eight gilt-silver jeweled hairpin flowers on top, two gilt-silver pheasants, and two pearl knot pendants held in the beak.

sentences.zh: 七品，霞帔、墜子、褙子與六品同。

translations.literal: Seventh rank, cloud collar, pendant, over-jacket same as sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh rank: the cloud collar, pendant, and over-jacket were the same as sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 八品、九品，霞帔用繡纏枝花，墜子與七品同，褙子繡摘枝團花。

translations.literal: Eighth and ninth ranks, cloud collar used embroidered entwined-branch flowers, pendant same as seventh rank, over-jacket embroidered plucked-branch round flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth and ninth ranks: the cloud collar was embroidered with entwined floral sprays; the pendant was the same as seventh rank; the over-jacket bore plucked-branch round floral medallions.

sentences.zh: 內外官親屬冠服：洪武元年，禮部尚書崔亮奉詔議定。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials' kin crowns and robes: Hongwu first year, Minister of Rites Cui Liang received edict to deliberate and fix.
translations.idiomatic: Crowns and robes for the kin of inner and outer officials: in the first year of Hongwu, Minister of Rites Cui Liang was ordered to deliberate and set the regulations.

sentences.zh: 內外官父、兄、伯、叔、子、孫、弟、侄用烏紗帽，軟腳垂帶，圓領衣，烏角帶。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials' fathers, elder brothers, uncles, younger brothers, nephews, sons, and grandsons used black gauze caps, soft flaps with hanging bands, round-collar robes, and black horn belts.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers, elder brothers, uncles, younger brothers, nephews, sons, and grandsons of inner and outer officials wore black gauze caps with soft hanging flaps, round-collar robes, and black horn belts.

sentences.zh: 品官祖母及母、與子孫同居親弟侄婦女禮服，合以本官所居官職品級，通用漆紗珠翠慶雲冠，本品衫，霞帔、褙子，緣襈襖裙，惟山鬆特髻子止許受封誥敕者用之。

translations.literal: Ranked officials' grandmothers and mothers, and daughters-in-law of sons and grandsons living in the same household, plus close younger brothers' and nephews' wives—ceremonial dress collectively used their official's rank, generally using lacquered gauze pearl-and-kingfisher auspicious-cloud crowns, rank-appropriate robes, cloud collars and over-jackets, bordered jacket-and-skirt sets; only the mountain-loose special bun was permitted for those who had received enfeoffment patents.
translations.idiomatic: For the grandmothers and mothers of ranked officials, and for daughters-in-law of sons and grandsons in the same household, together with wives of close younger brothers and nephews, ceremonial dress followed the husband's or son's official rank: lacquered gauze pearl-and-kingfisher auspicious-cloud crowns, rank-appropriate robes, cloud collars, over-jackets, and bordered jacket-and-skirt sets. The mountain-loose special bun was permitted only for women who had received patents of enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 品官次妻，許用本品珠翠慶雲冠、褙子為禮服。

translations.literal: Ranked officials' secondary wives permitted to use their husband's rank pearl-and-kingfisher auspicious-cloud crown and over-jacket as ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary wives of ranked officials were allowed to wear pearl-and-kingfisher auspicious-cloud crowns and over-jackets of their husband's rank as ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 銷金闊領、長襖長裙為常服。

translations.literal: Gilded wide-collar long jacket and long skirt as everyday dress.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress consisted of a gilded wide-collar long jacket and long skirt.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，令文武官父兄、伯叔、弟侄、子婿，皆許穿靴。

translations.literal: Twenty-fifth year, ordered civil and military officials' fathers, elder brothers, uncles, younger brothers, nephews, and sons-in-law—all permitted to wear boots.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, fathers, elder brothers, uncles, younger brothers, nephews, and sons-in-law of civil and military officials were all permitted to wear boots.

sentences.zh: 內使冠服：明初置內使監，冠烏紗描金曲腳帽，衣胸背花盤領窄袖衫，烏角帶，靴用紅扇面黑下樁。

translations.literal: Inner attendants' crowns and robes: early Ming established the Directorate of Palace Attendants; crown black gauze with gold-painted curved flaps; robe bore chest-and-back floral round-collar narrow-sleeved shirt; black horn belt; boots used red fan-face with black lower band.
translations.idiomatic: Crowns and robes of inner attendants: in the early Ming the Directorate of Palace Attendants was established. They wore black gauze caps with gold-painted curved flaps, narrow-sleeved round-collar shirts bearing chest-and-back floral panels, black horn belts, and boots with red vamps and black counters.

sentences.zh: 各宮火者，服與庶人同。

translations.literal: Fire-tenders of each palace, dress same as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Fire-tenders in the various palaces dressed the same as commoners.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年諭宰臣，內使監未有職名者，當別制冠，以別監官。

translations.literal: Hongwu third year instructed chief ministers, inner attendants of the directorate without official titles should have a separate crown design to distinguish them from directorate officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu the emperor instructed his chief ministers that unattached attendants of the directorate should wear a distinct cap to distinguish them from ranked directorate officials.

sentences.zh: 禮部奏定，內使監凡遇朝會，依品具朝服、公服行禮。

translations.literal: Ministry of Rites memorialized and fixed: the Directorate of Palace Attendants, whenever attending court assemblies, according to rank fully wore court dress and uniform robes to perform rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites submitted regulations: whenever the directorate attended court assemblies, its members wore court dress and uniform robes appropriate to their ranks.

sentences.zh: 其常服，葵花胸背團領衫，不拘顏色；

translations.literal: Their everyday dress, sunflower chest-and-back round-collar shirt, not restricted in color;
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress was a round-collar shirt with sunflower chest-and-back panels, without restriction on color;

sentences.zh: 烏紗帽；

translations.literal: black gauze cap;
translations.idiomatic: a black gauze cap;

sentences.zh: 犀角帶。

translations.literal: rhinoceros-horn belt.
translations.idiomatic: and a rhinoceros-horn belt.

sentences.zh: 無品從者，常服團領衫，無胸背花，不拘顏色；

translations.literal: Unranked attendants, everyday dress round-collar shirt, no chest-and-back floral panels, not restricted in color;
translations.idiomatic: Unranked attendants wore round-collar shirts without chest-and-back panels, in any color;

sentences.zh: 烏角帶；

translations.literal: black horn belt;
translations.idiomatic: black horn belts;

sentences.zh: 烏紗帽，垂軟帶。

translations.literal: black gauze cap, hanging soft bands.
translations.idiomatic: black gauze caps with soft hanging bands.

sentences.zh: 年十五以下者，惟戴烏紗小頂帽。

translations.literal: Those fifteen years of age and below, only wore black gauze small-topped caps.
translations.idiomatic: Those fifteen or younger wore only small-topped black gauze caps.

sentences.zh: 按《大政記》，永樂以後，宦官在帝左右，必蟒服，制如曳撒，繡蟒於左右，系以鸞帶，此燕閑之服也。

translations.literal: According to the Record of Major Policies, after Yongle eunuchs at the emperor's side invariably wore python robes, made like yisagu, with pythons embroidered left and right, secured with gold phoenix belts—this was informal dress.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Record of Major Policies, after the Yongle reign eunuchs at the emperor's side invariably wore python robes cut like yisagu coats, with pythons embroidered on either side and secured with phoenix belts—informal dress.

sentences.zh: 次則飛魚，惟入侍用之。

translations.literal: Next came flying-fish robes, used only when entering attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Next in rank were flying-fish robes, worn only when entering attendance on the emperor.

sentences.zh: 貴而用事者，賜蟒，文武一品官所不易得也。

translations.literal: Those who were eminent and wielded power were granted python robes—what even civil and military officials of first rank could not easily obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful eunuchs of high standing were granted python robes—a privilege not easily granted even to civil and military officials of first rank.

sentences.zh: 單蟒面皆斜向，坐蟒則面正向，尤貴。

translations.literal: Single pythons on the face all faced obliquely; seated pythons faced directly forward—especially prized.
translations.idiomatic: On single-python robes the beasts all faced obliquely; on seated-python robes they faced directly forward—the latter especially prized.

sentences.zh: 又有膝衤闌者，亦如曳撒，上有蟒補，當膝處橫織細雲蟒，蓋南郊及山陵扈從，便於乘馬也。

translations.literal: There were also knee-kilt robes, likewise like yisagu, with python patches above; at the knee horizontal fine cloud python weaving, for escorting at the Southern Suburban Altar and imperial tombs, convenient for riding horseback.
translations.idiomatic: There were also knee-kilt robes, likewise cut like yisagu, with python patches above and fine horizontal cloud-pythons woven at the knee—garments for escorting the emperor at the Southern Suburban Altar and at imperial tombs, where ease on horseback mattered.

sentences.zh: 或召對燕見，君臣皆不用袍而用此；

translations.literal: When summoned for audience or informal meetings, emperor and ministers alike forwent formal robes and wore these instead;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor summoned his ministers for audience or informal meetings, both sides often wore these rather than formal robes;

sentences.zh: 第蟒有五爪、四爪之分，襴有紅、黃之別耳。

translations.literal: only pythons had five-claw and four-claw distinctions, and kilts had red and yellow variants.
translations.idiomatic: only the pythons differed as five-claw or four-claw, and the kilts as red or yellow.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年，都御史邊鏞言：「國朝品官無蟒衣之制。

translations.literal: Hongzhi first year, Censor-in-chief Bian Yong said: "Our dynasty's ranked officials have no python-robe regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongzhi, Censor-in-chief Bian Yong said, "Ranked officials of our dynasty have no prescribed python robes.

sentences.zh: 夫蟒無角、無足，今內官多乞蟒衣，殊類龍形，非制也。

translations.literal: Pythons have no horns and no feet; now many inner attendants beg for python robes, greatly resembling dragon form—not according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Pythons have neither horns nor feet, yet many inner attendants now petition for python robes that greatly resemble dragons. This is not according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 」乃下詔禁之。

translations.literal: "Thereupon an edict prohibited it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued forbidding the practice.

sentences.zh: 十七年，諭閣臣劉健曰：「內臣僭妄尤多。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year, instructed Grand Secretary Liu Jian, saying: "Inner attendants' presumptuous excesses are especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the emperor instructed Grand Secretary Liu Jian, saying, "The presumptuous excesses of inner attendants are especially numerous.

sentences.zh: 」因言服色所宜禁，曰：「蟒、龍、飛魚、斗牛，本在所禁，不合私織。

translations.literal: "Thereupon spoke of dress colors that ought to be forbidden, saying: "Python, dragon, flying fish, and bull-fight patterns are originally among the forbidden—private weaving is not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He then spoke of forbidden dress colors, saying, "Pythons, dragons, flying fish, and bull-fight patterns are among the categories expressly forbidden; they must not be woven privately.

sentences.zh: 間有賜者，或久而敝，不宜輒自織用。

translations.literal: Occasionally some are granted by bestowal; when old and worn they should not be casually rewoven for use.
translations.idiomatic: Occasionally robes are granted by imperial bestowal; when these grow old and worn, attendants should not casually have new ones woven for themselves.

sentences.zh: 玄、黃、紫、皁乃屬正禁，即柳黃、明黃、薑黃諸色，亦應禁之。

translations.literal: Black, yellow, purple, and dark brown belong to the strictly forbidden; even willow yellow, bright yellow, and ginger yellow should also be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Black, yellow, purple, and dark brown are strictly forbidden; even willow yellow, bright yellow, and ginger yellow ought to be banned.

sentences.zh: 」孝宗加意鉗束，故申飭者再，然內官驕姿已久，積習相沿，不能止也。

translations.literal: "Emperor Xiaozong applied himself keenly to restraint, hence the repeated admonitions, yet inner attendants had long been arrogant and the accumulated custom persisted—it could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong applied himself keenly to restraint, and so issued these repeated admonitions, yet inner attendants had long been arrogant and old habits endured—the practice could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖制內臣服，其紗帽與羣臣異，且無朝冠、襆頭，亦無祭服。

translations.literal: Initially, Taizu fixed inner-attendant dress; their gauze caps differed from ministers', and they had neither court crowns nor futou, nor sacrificial dress.
translations.idiomatic: At first Taizu fixed dress for inner attendants: their gauze caps differed from those of ministers, and they had neither court crowns, nor futou, nor sacrificial robes.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，穆宗主入太廟，大榼冠進賢，服祭服以從，蓋內府祀中霤、竈井之神，例遣中官，因自創為祭服，非由廷議也。

translations.literal: Early Wanli, when Emperor Muzong as ruler entered the Imperial Ancestral Temple, large-frame jinxian caps and sacrificial robes to follow—because the inner palace dispatched central attendants to sacrifice to the gods of the central drain, stove, and well by precedent, and so they created sacrificial dress for themselves, not by court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wanli period, when Emperor Muzong entered the Imperial Ancestral Temple as ruling sovereign, eunuchs followed in large-frame jinxian caps and sacrificial robes. The inner palace routinely dispatched central attendants to sacrifice to the gods of the central drain, stove, and well, and on that precedent they devised sacrificial dress for themselves—not by deliberation of the court.

sentences.zh: 侍儀舍人冠服：洪武二年，禮官議定。

translations.literal: Ceremonial attendants' crowns and robes: Hongwu second year, ritual officials deliberated and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Crowns and robes of ceremonial attendants: in the second year of Hongwu, ritual officials deliberated and fixed the regulations.

sentences.zh: 侍儀舍人導禮，依元制，展腳襆頭，窄袖紫衫，塗金束帶，皁紋靴。

translations.literal: Ceremonial attendants guided rites, following Yuan regulations: extended-flap futou, narrow-sleeved purple shirts, gilded belts, black-pattern boots.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial attendants guided ritual proceedings. Following Yuan precedent, they wore extended-flap futou, narrow-sleeved purple shirts, gilded belts, and black-pattern boots.

sentences.zh: 常服：烏紗唐帽，諸色盤領衫，烏角束帶，衫不用黃。

translations.literal: Everyday dress: black gauze Tang caps, various-colored round-collar shirts, black horn belts; shirts did not use yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress: black gauze Tang caps, round-collar shirts in various colors, and black horn belts; yellow was not permitted for the shirts.

sentences.zh: 四年，中書省議定，侍儀舍人並御史臺知班，引禮執事，冠進賢冠，無樑，服絳色衣，其蔽膝、履、襪、帶、笏，與九品同，惟不用中單。

translations.literal: Fourth year, the Secretariat deliberated and fixed: ceremonial attendants together with the Censorate's rank-knowers, who guided ritual and served as attendants, wore jinxian crowns without crossbar, crimson robes; their apron panels, shoes, socks, belts, and tablets were the same as ninth rank, except they did not use the inner undergarment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Secretariat fixed regulations: ceremonial attendants, together with the Censorate's rank-knowers who guided ritual proceedings, wore jinxian crowns without crossbars and crimson robes; their apron panels, shoes, socks, belts, and tablets matched ninth rank, except that they did not wear the inner undergarment.

sentences.zh: 校尉冠服：洪武三年定制，執仗之士，首服皆縷金額交腳襆頭，其服有諸色辟邪、寶相花裙襖，銅葵花束帶，皁紋靴。

translations.literal: Guard officers' crowns and robes: Hongwu third year fixed regulations; men bearing staves all wore gold-threaded foreheads with crossed-flap futou; their dress included various-colored demon-quelling and precious-flower skirt-jackets, copper sunflower belts, black-pattern boots.
translations.idiomatic: Crowns and robes of guard officers: fixed in the third year of Hongwu. Bearers of ceremonial staves all wore crossed-flap futou with gold-threaded foreheads; their dress included skirt-jackets in various colors bearing demon-quelling and precious-flower motifs, copper sunflower belts, and black-pattern boots.

sentences.zh: 六年，令校尉衣只孫，束帶，襆頭，靴鞋。

translations.literal: Sixth year, ordered guard officers' dress to zhisun, belt, futou, boots and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year guard officers were ordered to wear zhisun robes, belts, futou, and boots or shoes.

sentences.zh: 只孫，一作質孫，本元制，蓋一色衣也。

translations.literal: Zhisun, also written zhitu-sun, originally Yuan system—essentially a single-color garment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhisun—also written zhitu-sun—was originally a Yuan institution: essentially a one-color garment.

sentences.zh: 十四年改用金鵝帽，黑漆戧金荔枝銅釘樣，每五釘攢就，四面稍起邊襴，鞓青緊束之。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year changed to gold-goose caps, black lacquer raised-gold lychee and copper-nail pattern, every five nails clustered together, four sides slightly raised with bordering kilt, green band tightly bound.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year they changed to gold-goose caps: black lacquer with raised-gold lychee-and-copper-nail patterns, every five nails clustered together, with slightly raised bordering on all four sides, tightly bound with a green sash.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，令將軍、力士、校尉、旗軍常戴頭巾或榼腦。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year, ordered generals, strongmen, guard officers, and banner soldiers routinely to wear headcloths or ke-nao caps.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year generals, strongmen, guard officers, and banner soldiers were ordered routinely to wear headcloths or ke-nao caps.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，令校尉、力士上直穿靴，出外不許。

translations.literal: Twenty-fifth year, ordered guard officers and strongmen on palace duty to wear boots; going out not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year guard officers and strongmen on palace duty were permitted to wear boots, but not when going out in public.

sentences.zh: 刻期冠服：宋置快行親從官，明初謂之刻期。

translations.literal: Qieqi runners' crowns and robes: Song established fast-travel personal attendants; early Ming called them qieqi.
translations.idiomatic: Crowns and robes of qieqi runners: the Song established fast-travel personal attendants; in the early Ming they were called qieqi.

sentences.zh: 冠方頂巾，衣胸背鷹鷂，花腰，線襖子，諸色闊匾絲絛，大象牙雕花環，行縢八帶鞋。

translations.literal: Crown square-topped cloth; robe chest-and-back hawk-kite, floral waist, thread jacket, various-colored broad flat silk sash, large ivory carved floral ring, eight-band leg-wrapping shoes.
translations.idiomatic: They wore square-topped cloth caps, robes with hawk-and-kite chest-and-back panels, floral waistbands, thread jackets, broad flat silk sashes in various colors, large carved ivory sash rings, and eight-band leg-wrapping shoes.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年，惟用雕刻象牙絛環，餘同庶民。

translations.literal: Hongwu sixth year, only used carved ivory sash rings; remainder same as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Hongwu they were restricted to carved ivory sash rings; otherwise their dress was the same as commoners'.

sentences.zh: 儒士、生員、監生巾服：洪武三年，令士人戴四方平定巾。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars, students, and Imperial Academy students' caps and robes: Hongwu third year, ordered scholars to wear the Square Peace cap.
translations.idiomatic: Caps and robes of Confucian scholars, students, and Imperial Academy students: in the third year of Hongwu scholars were ordered to wear the Square Peace cap.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，定儒士、生員衣，自領至裳，去地一寸，袖長過手，復回不及肘三寸。

translations.literal: Twenty-third year, fixed scholars' and students' robes: from collar to skirt hem one inch from the ground; sleeves long past the hands, turning back not reaching three inches above the elbow.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year regulations fixed scholars' and students' robes: from collar to hem one inch above the ground; sleeves extending past the hands, turned back to no more than three inches above the elbow.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以士子巾服，無異吏胥，宜甄別之，命工部制式以進。

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth year, because scholars' caps and robes differed little from clerks and petty officials, distinction was desirable; ordered the Ministry of Works to prepare models for submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, because scholars' caps and robes differed little from those of clerks and runners, distinction was needed; the Ministry of Works was ordered to prepare models for the emperor's review.

sentences.zh: 太祖親視，凡三易乃定。

translations.literal: Taizu personally inspected them; only after three revisions were they fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu inspected them in person, and only after three revisions were the forms fixed.

sentences.zh: 生員襴衫，用玉色布絹為之，寬袖皁緣，皁絛軟巾垂帶。

translations.literal: Students' kilt-robes made of jade-colored cloth or silk, wide sleeves with black borders, black sash, soft cloth cap with hanging bands.
translations.idiomatic: Students wore kilt-robes of jade-colored cloth or silk, with wide sleeves and black borders, black sashes, and soft cloth caps with hanging bands.

sentences.zh: 貢舉入監者，不變所服。

translations.literal: Those entering the academy by tribute examination did not change what they wore.
translations.idiomatic: Those entering the academy through the tribute examination kept the dress they already wore.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，許戴遮陽帽，後遂私戴之。

translations.literal: Late Hongwu, sun-shade caps were permitted; afterward people wore them privately.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Hongwu period sun-shade caps were permitted; afterward people wore them without authorization.

sentences.zh: 洪熙中，帝問衣藍者何人，左右以監生對。

translations.literal: In the Hongxi reign the emperor asked who those in blue clothes were; those at his side answered that they were academy students.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongxi reign the emperor asked who the men in blue robes were; his attendants replied that they were academy students.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「著青衣較好。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wearing green would be better.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Green would look better.

sentences.zh: 」乃易青圓領。

translations.literal: "Thereupon changed to green round-collar robes.
translations.idiomatic: The robes were changed to green round-collar garments.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十二年，禮部言士子冠服詭異，有淩雲等巾，甚乖禮制，詔所司禁之。

translations.literal: Jiajing twenty-second year, Ministry of Rites said scholars' caps and robes had grown bizarre, with Lingyun and other caps, greatly at odds with ritual regulation; an edict ordered the authorities to forbid them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Jiajing the Ministry of Rites reported that scholars' caps and robes had grown bizarre, including Lingyun and other irregular caps greatly at odds with ritual regulation; an edict ordered the authorities to forbid them.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年禁舉人、監生、生儒僭用忠靜冠巾，錦綺鑲履及張傘蓋，戴暖耳，違者五城御史送問。

translations.literal: Wanli second year forbade tribute scholars, academy students, and literati from presumptuously using Zhongjing caps and cloth, brocade-and-silk embroidered shoes, parasols and canopies, and warm ear-covers; violators were seized by the Five-District censors for inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wanli, tribute scholars, academy students, and literati were forbidden to wear presumptuously Zhongjing caps and cloth, brocade-embroidered shoes, parasols and canopies, or warm ear-covers; violators were seized by censors of the Five Districts for inquiry.

sentences.zh: 庶人冠服：明初，庶人婚，許假九品服。

translations.literal: Commoners' crowns and robes: early Ming, commoners at marriage permitted to borrow ninth-rank dress.
translations.idiomatic: Crowns and robes of commoners: in the early Ming, commoners at marriage were permitted to borrow ninth-rank dress.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，庶人初戴四帶巾，改四方平定巾，雜色盤領衣，不許用黃。

translations.literal: Hongwu third year, commoners at first wore four-band caps, changed to Square Peace caps, miscellaneous-colored round-collar robes, not permitted to use yellow.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu commoners at first wore four-band caps, then changed to Square Peace caps and round-collar robes in miscellaneous colors; yellow was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 又令男女衣服，不得僭用金繡、錦綺、紵絲、綾羅，止許槹、絹、素紗，其靴不得裁製花樣、金線裝飾。

translations.literal: Also ordered men's and women's clothes not presumptuously to use gold embroidery, brocade, ramie silk, damask, or gauze; only ramie, silk, and plain gauze permitted; boots could not be cut with floral patterns or gold-thread ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations also forbade men and women from wearing gold embroidery, brocade, ramie silk, damask, or gauze, limiting them to ramie, silk, and plain gauze; boots could not be cut with floral patterns or trimmed with gold thread.

sentences.zh: 首飾、釵、鐲不許用金玉、珠翠，止用銀。

translations.literal: Head ornaments, hairpins, and bracelets not permitted to use gold, jade, or kingfisher; only silver permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Head ornaments, hairpins, and bracelets could not use gold, jade, or kingfisher feathers—only silver.

sentences.zh: 六年，令庶人巾環不得用金玉、瑪瑙、珊瑚、琥珀。

translations.literal: Sixth year, ordered commoners' cap rings not to use gold, jade, agate, coral, or amber.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year commoners were forbidden cap rings of gold, jade, agate, coral, or amber.

sentences.zh: 未入流品者同。

translations.literal: Those not entered in the rank rolls were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Those not entered in the rank rolls were subject to the same rules.

sentences.zh: 庶人帽，不得用頂，帽珠止許水晶、香木。

translations.literal: Commoners' caps could not use domed tops; cap beads permitted only crystal and fragrant wood.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners' caps could not have domed tops; cap beads were limited to crystal and fragrant wood.

sentences.zh: 十四年令農衣槹、紗、絹、布，商賈止衣絹、布。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year ordered farmers' clothing ramie, gauze, silk, and cloth; merchants and traders only silk and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year farmers were permitted ramie, gauze, silk, and cloth; merchants and traders only silk and cloth.

sentences.zh: 農家有一人為商賈者，亦不得衣槹、紗。

translations.literal: Farm households with one member engaged in trade could not wear ramie or gauze either.
translations.idiomatic: In farm households where one member engaged in trade, even farmers could not wear ramie or gauze.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，令農夫戴斗笠、蒲笠出入市井不禁，不親農業者不許。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year, ordered farmers to wear bamboo hats or sedge-leaf hats in markets and streets without prohibition; those not engaged in agriculture were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year farmers were permitted to wear bamboo or sedge-leaf hats in markets and streets without penalty; those not engaged in farming were not.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，令耆民衣制，袖長過手，復回不及肘三寸；

translations.literal: Twenty-third year, ordered elders' clothing: sleeves long past the hands, turning back not reaching three inches above the elbow;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year regulations for elders' dress fixed sleeves extending past the hands, turned back to no more than three inches above the elbow;

sentences.zh: 庶人衣長去地五寸，袖長過手六寸，袖樁廣一尺，袖口五寸。

translations.literal: Commoners' robes one length five inches from the ground, sleeves long past the hands six inches, sleeve band one foot wide, cuff opening five inches.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners' robes hung one hand-span above the ground, with sleeves extending six inches past the hands, sleeve bands one foot wide, and cuff openings five inches.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以民間違禁，靴巧裁花樣，嵌以金線藍條，詔禮部嚴禁庶人不許穿靴，止許穿皮劄鵓翁，惟北地苦寒，許用牛皮直縫靴。

translations.literal: Twenty-fifth year, because among the people violations proliferated—boots artfully cut with floral patterns inlaid with gold-thread blue bands—an edict ordered the Ministry of Rites strictly to forbid commoners from wearing boots, permitting only leather pazhabo boots; only in the cold north were straight-seamed cowhide boots permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, because violations had proliferated—boots artfully cut with floral patterns and inlaid with gold-thread blue bands—an edict ordered the Ministry of Rites strictly to forbid commoners from wearing boots, allowing only simple leather pazhabo boots; in the cold north alone straight-seamed cowhide boots were permitted.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，禁商販、僕役、倡優、下賤不許服用貂裘。

translations.literal: Zhengde first year, forbade merchants, servants, actors, and baseborn people from wearing sable fur.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde merchants, servants, actors, and people of base birth were forbidden to wear sable fur.

sentences.zh: 十六年，禁軍民衣紫花罩甲，或禁門或四外遊走者，緝事人擒之。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, forbade soldiers and civilians from wearing purple floral sleeveless armor; anyone seen at forbidden gates or wandering outside was seized by surveillance officers.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year soldiers and civilians were forbidden purple floral sleeveless armor; surveillance officers were to seize anyone wearing it at forbidden gates or wandering abroad.

sentences.zh: 士庶妻冠服：洪武三年定制，士庶妻，首飾用銀鍍金，耳環用金珠，釧鐲用銀，服淺色團衫，用紵絲、綾羅、槹絹。

translations.literal: Wives of scholars and commoners' crowns and robes: Hongwu third year fixed regulations; wives of scholars and commoners, head ornaments used silver with gold plating, earrings used gold beads, bracelets and armlets used silver, dress light-colored round shirts, using ramie silk, damask, gauze, ramie.
translations.idiomatic: Crowns and robes of scholars' and commoners' wives: fixed in the third year of Hongwu. Their head ornaments were silver with gold plating; earrings were gold beads; bracelets and armlets were silver; dress was light-colored round shirts of ramie silk, damask, gauze, or ramie.

sentences.zh: 五年，令民間婦人禮服惟紫絁，不用金繡，袍衫止紫、綠、桃紅及諸淺淡顏色，不許用大紅、鴉青、黃色，帶用藍絹布。

translations.literal: Fifth year, ordered commoners' women's ceremonial dress only purple woven silk, no gold embroidery; robes and shirts only purple, green, peach pink, and other pale colors—not permitted large red, crow blue, or yellow; sashes used blue silk cloth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year commoners' wives were limited to purple woven silk for ceremonial dress, without gold embroidery; robes and shirts to purple, green, peach pink, and other pale colors—never large red, crow blue, or yellow; sashes were of blue silk cloth.

sentences.zh: 女子在室者，作三小髻，金釵，珠頭閟窄袖褙子。

translations.literal: Unmarried women wore three small buns, gold hairpins, pearl headpieces, narrow-sleeved over-jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Unmarried women wore three small buns, gold hairpins, pearl headpieces, and narrow-sleeved over-jackets.

sentences.zh: 凡婢使，高頂髻，絹布狹領長襖，長裙。

translations.literal: All maidservants, high topknots, silk-or-cloth narrow-collar long jackets, long skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Maidservants wore high topknots, narrow-collar long jackets of silk or cloth, and long skirts.

sentences.zh: 小婢使，雙髻，長袖短衣，長裙。

translations.literal: Junior maidservants, double buns, long-sleeved short jackets, long skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Junior maidservants wore double buns, long-sleeved short jackets, and long skirts.

sentences.zh: 成化十年，禁官民婦女不得僭用渾金衣服，寶石首飾。

translations.literal: Chenghua tenth year, forbade officials' and commoners' wives from presumptuously using solid-gold clothing and gemstone head ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Chenghua officials' and commoners' wives were forbidden to wear solid-gold clothing or gemstone head ornaments.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，令軍民婦女不許用銷金衣服、帳幔，寶石首飾、鐲釧。

translations.literal: Zhengde first year, ordered soldiers' and civilians' wives not to use gilded clothing, hangings, gemstone head ornaments, bracelets, or armlets.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde soldiers' and civilians' wives were forbidden gilded clothing and hangings, gemstone head ornaments, bracelets, and armlets.

sentences.zh: 協律郎、樂舞生冠服：明初，郊社宗廟用雅樂，協律郎襆頭，紫羅袍，荔枝帶；

translations.literal: Music-master and ritual dancers' crowns and robes: early Ming, suburban, ancestral, and temple rites used elegant music; music-master wore futou, purple gauze robe, lychee belt;
translations.idiomatic: Crowns and robes of music-masters and ritual dancers: in the early Ming, suburban, ancestral, and temple rites used elegant music. The music-master wore futou, a purple gauze robe, and a lychee belt;

sentences.zh: 樂生緋袍，展腳襆頭；

translations.literal: Dancers wore crimson robes, extended-flap futou;
translations.idiomatic: Dancers wore crimson robes and extended-flap futou;

sentences.zh: 舞士襆頭，紅羅袍，荔枝帶，皁靴；

translations.literal: Dance performers, futou, red gauze robes, lychee belts, black boots;
translations.idiomatic: Dance performers wore futou, red gauze robes, lychee belts, and black boots;

sentences.zh: 文舞生紅袍，武舞生緋袍，俱展腳襆頭，革帶，皁靴。

translations.literal: Civil dance students red robes, martial dance students crimson robes, all extended-flap futou, leather belts, black boots.
translations.idiomatic: Civil dance students wore red robes and martial dance students crimson robes, all with extended-flap futou, leather belts, and black boots.

sentences.zh: 朝會大樂九奏歌工：中華一統巾，紅羅生色大袖衫，畫黃鶯、鸚鵡花樣，紅生絹襯衫，錦領，杏紅絹裙，白絹大口袴，青絲絛，白絹襪，茶褐鞋。

translations.literal: Court assembly great music nine movements singers: Single Zhonghua cap, red gauze patterned large-sleeved jackets painted with oriole and parrot designs, red raw-silk under-jackets, brocade collars, apricot-red silk skirts, white silk wide trousers, green silk sashes, white silk socks, tea-brown shoes.
translations.idiomatic: For the nine movements of great music at court assemblies, singers wore the Single Zhonghua cap, red gauze patterned large-sleeved jackets painted with oriole and parrot designs, red raw-silk under-jackets, brocade collars, apricot-red silk skirts, white silk wide trousers, green silk sashes, white silk socks, and tea-brown shoes.

sentences.zh: 其和聲郎押樂者：皁羅闊帶巾，青羅大袖衫，紅生絹襯衫，錦領，塗金束帶，皁靴。

translations.literal: The harmony masters who conducted the music: black gauze broad-ribbon caps, blue gauze large-sleeved jackets, red raw-silk under-jackets, brocade collars, gilt waist-belts, black boots.
translations.idiomatic: The harmony masters who conducted the music wore black gauze broad-ribbon caps, blue gauze large-sleeved jackets, red raw-silk under-jackets, brocade collars, gilt waist-belts, and black boots.

sentences.zh: 其三舞：

translations.literal: The three dances:
translations.idiomatic: The three dances were as follows:

sentences.zh: 一、武舞，曰《平定天下之舞》。

translations.literal: First, martial dance, called "The Dance of Pacifying All Under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: First, the martial dance, called "The Dance of Pacifying All Under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 舞士皆黃金束發冠，紫絲纓，青羅生色畫舞鶴花樣窄袖衫，白生絹襯衫，錦領、紅羅銷金大袖罩袍，紅羅銷金裙，皁生色畫花緣襈，白羅銷金汗袴，藍青羅銷金緣，紅絹擁項，紅結子，紅絹束腰，塗金束帶，青絲大絛，錦臂韝，綠雲頭皁靴。

translations.literal: All dance performers wore gold hair-binding crowns, purple silk tassels, blue gauze patterned narrow-sleeved jackets painted with dancing-crane designs, white raw-silk under-jackets, brocade collars, red gauze gold-cutwork large-sleeved outer robes, red gauze gold-cutwork skirts, black patterned jackets with painted floral borders, white gauze gold-cutwork fitted trousers, blue-green gauze gold-cutwork borders, red silk neck wraps, red knot ornaments, red silk waist bindings, gilt waist-belts, green silk great sashes, brocade arm guards, and black boots with green cloud-toe caps.
translations.idiomatic: All dance performers wore gold hair-binding crowns with purple silk tassels, blue gauze patterned narrow-sleeved jackets painted with dancing cranes, white raw-silk under-jackets, brocade collars, red gauze gold-cutwork large-sleeved outer robes and skirts, black patterned jackets with painted floral borders, white gauze gold-cutwork fitted trousers with blue-green gauze gold-cutwork borders, red silk neck wraps and knot ornaments, red silk waist bindings, gilt waist-belts, green silk great sashes, brocade arm guards, and black boots with green cloud-toe caps.

sentences.zh: 舞師，黃金束發冠，紫絲纓，青羅大袖衫，白絹襯衫，錦領，塗金束帶，綠雲頭皁靴。

translations.literal: Dance masters, gold hair-binding crowns, purple silk tassels, blue gauze large-sleeved jackets, white silk under-jackets, brocade collars, gilt waist-belts, green cloud-toe black boots.
translations.idiomatic: Dance masters wore gold hair-binding crowns with purple silk tassels, blue gauze large-sleeved jackets, white silk under-jackets, brocade collars, gilt waist-belts, and black boots with green cloud-toe caps.

sentences.zh: 一、文舞，曰《車書會同之舞》。

translations.literal: One, civil dance, called "The Dance of Chariots and Script in Universal Harmony."
translations.idiomatic: Second, the civil dance, called "The Dance of Chariots and Script in Universal Harmony."

sentences.zh: 舞士皆黑光描金方山冠，青絲纓，紅羅大袖衫，紅生絹襯衫，錦領，紅羅擁項，紅結子，塗金束帶，白絹大口袴，白絹襪，茶褐鞋。

translations.literal: All dance performers wore lacquered-black gold-traced square mountain crowns, green silk tassels, red gauze large-sleeved jackets, red raw-silk under-jackets, brocade collars, red gauze neck wraps, red knot ornaments, gilt waist-belts, white silk wide trousers, white silk socks, tea-brown shoes.
translations.idiomatic: All dance performers wore lacquered-black gold-traced square mountain crowns with green silk tassels, red gauze large-sleeved jackets, red raw-silk under-jackets, brocade collars, red gauze neck wraps and knot ornaments, gilt waist-belts, white silk wide trousers, white silk socks, and tea-brown shoes.

sentences.zh: 舞師冠服與舞士同，惟大袖衫用青羅，不用紅羅擁項、紅結子。

translations.literal: Dance masters' crowns and dress matched the dance performers, except that the large-sleeved jackets were of blue gauze, without red gauze neck wraps or red knot ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Dance masters wore the same crowns and dress as the performers, except that their large-sleeved jackets were of blue gauze and they did without red gauze neck wraps or red knot ornaments.

sentences.zh: 一、文舞，曰《撫安四夷之舞》。

translations.literal: One, civil dance, called "The Dance of Pacifying the Four Barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Third, the civil dance, called "The Dance of Pacifying the Four Barbarians."

sentences.zh: 舞士，東夷四人，椎髻於後，系紅銷金頭繩，紅羅銷金抹額，中綴塗金博山，兩傍綴塗金巾環，明金耳環，青羅生色畫花大袖衫，紅生色領袖，紅羅銷金裙，青銷金裙緣，紅生絹襯衫，錦領，塗金束帶，烏皮靴。

translations.literal: Dance performers, four Eastern Yi: topknots at the back, red gold-cutwork head cords, red gauze gold-cutwork forehead bands with gilt Bo Mountain ornaments at the center and gilt cap rings on either side, bright-gold earrings, blue gauze patterned painted floral large-sleeved jackets, red patterned collars and sleeves, red gauze gold-cutwork skirts, blue gold-cutwork skirt borders, red raw-silk under-jackets, brocade collars, gilt waist-belts, black leather boots.
translations.idiomatic: Four Eastern Yi dancers wore topknots at the back, red gold-cutwork head cords, red gauze gold-cutwork forehead bands centered with gilt Bo Mountain ornaments and gilt cap rings on either side, bright-gold earrings, blue gauze patterned painted floral large-sleeved jackets with red patterned collars and sleeves, red gauze gold-cutwork skirts with blue gold-cutwork borders, red raw-silk under-jackets, brocade collars, gilt waist-belts, and black leather boots.

sentences.zh: 西戎四人，間道錦纏頭，明金耳環，紅紵絲細摺襖子，大紅羅生色雲肩，綠生色緣，藍青羅銷金汗袴，紅銷金緣繫腰合缽，十字泥金數珠，五色銷金羅香囊，紅絹擁項，紅結子，赤皮靴。

translations.literal: Four Western Rong: striped brocade head wraps, bright-gold earrings, red ramie fine-pleated jackets, large red gauze patterned cloud-shoulders, green patterned borders, blue-green gauze gold-cutwork fitted trousers, red gold-cutwork border waist girdles, ten-string gilt prayer beads, five-color gold-cutwork gauze incense pouches, red silk neck wraps, red knot ornaments, red leather boots.
translations.idiomatic: Four Western Rong dancers wore striped brocade head wraps and bright-gold earrings, red ramie fine-pleated jackets, large red gauze patterned cloud-shoulders with green patterned borders, blue-green gauze gold-cutwork fitted trousers, red gold-cutwork border waist girdles, ten-string gilt prayer beads, five-color gold-cutwork gauze incense pouches, red silk neck wraps and knot ornaments, and red leather boots.

sentences.zh: 南蠻四人，綰朝天髻，系紅羅生色銀錠，紅銷金抹額，明金耳環，紅織金短襖子，綠織金細摺短裙，絨錦袴，間道紵絲手巾，泥金頂牌，金珠瓔珞綴小金鈴，錦行纏，泥金獅蠻帶，綠銷金擁項，紅結子，赤皮靴。

translations.literal: Dancers' and musicians' dress colors matched the lead dancers.

translations.literal: Palace women's music crowns and dress: fixed in Hongwu third year.

translations.idiomatic: Directorate officials' everyday caps and belts matched those of the hundred officials;

translations.idiomatic: Performers, section chiefs, and musicians all wore black headcloths and multi-colored sashes.

translations.literal: Princely establishment musicians' crowns and dress: fixed in Hongwu fifteenth year.

sentences.zh: 十四年，令各衛門祗禁，原服皁衣改用淡青。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, ordered gate guards of each guard post, originally wearing black clothing, to change to pale blue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year gate guards of each guard post, who had originally worn black clothing, were ordered to change to pale blue.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，皁隸伴當不許著靴，止用皮劄鵓翁。

translations.literal: Twenty-fifth year, black-clad attendants were not permitted to wear boots, using only leather pazhabo boots.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year black-clad attendants were forbidden to wear boots and were limited to leather pazhabo boots.

sentences.zh: 外國君臣冠服：洪武二年，高麗入朝，請祭服制度，命制給之。

translations.literal: Foreign rulers and ministers' crowns and dress: Hongwu second year, Goryeo came to court and requested sacrificial dress regulations; they were ordered made and granted.
translations.idiomatic: Crowns and dress for foreign rulers and ministers: in the second year of Hongwu, when Goryeo came to court and requested sacrificial dress regulations, the court ordered them made and granted.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，定蕃國朝貢儀，國王來朝，如賞賜朝服者，服之以朝。

translations.literal: Twenty-seventh year, fixed tribute ceremony regulations for vassal states; when kings came to court, if granted court dress they wore it at audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year regulations for vassal tribute ceremonies were fixed: when kings came to court, if granted court dress they wore it at audience.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，賜琉球國王並其臣下冠服。

translations.literal: Thirty-first year, granted crowns and dress to the king of Ryukyu and his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year crowns and dress were granted to the king of Ryukyu and his ministers.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，賜琉球中山王皮弁、玉圭，麟袍、犀帶，視二品秩。

translations.literal: During Yongle, granted the Chungshan king of Ryukyu leather caps, jade tablets, python robes, rhinoceros belts, treated as second rank.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle the Chungshan king of Ryukyu was granted leather caps, jade tablets, python robes, and rhinoceros belts, treated as second rank.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年，朝鮮國王李濩言：「洪武中，蒙賜國王冕服九章，陪臣冠服比朝廷遞降二等，故陪臣一等比朝臣第三等，得五樑冠服。

translations.literal: Xuande third year, King Yi Hu of Joseon said: "In Hongwu we were granted the king's nine-emblem sacrificial dress; attendant ministers' crowns and dress were two ranks below the court, so first-rank attendants matched third-rank court officials and received five-ridge crowns and dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande King Yi Hu of Joseon said: "In Hongwu we were granted the king's nine-emblem sacrificial dress; attendant ministers' crowns and dress were two ranks below the court, so first-rank attendants matched third-rank court officials and received five-ridge crowns and dress.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，先臣芳遠遣世子禔入朝，蒙賜五樑冠服。

translations.literal: Early Yongle, my late father Pangyŏn sent the heir Ti to court, and he was granted five-ridge crowns and dress.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongle my late father Pangyŏn sent the heir Ti to court, and he was granted five-ridge crowns and dress.

sentences.zh: 臣竊惟世子冠服，何止同陪臣一等，乞為定制。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to consider that the heir's crowns and dress far exceed those of first-rank attendants; I beg that this be made a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject ventures to consider that the heir's crowns and dress far exceed those of first-rank attendants; I beg that this be made a fixed regulation.

sentences.zh: 」乃命制六樑冠賜之。

translations.literal: " The court then ordered a six-ridge crown made and granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The court then ordered a six-ridge crown made and granted.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年，令外國朝貢入，不許擅用違製衣服。

translations.literal: Jiajing sixth year, ordered that foreign tribute missions entering court were not permitted to use unauthorized dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiajing foreign tribute missions entering court were forbidden to use unauthorized dress.

sentences.zh: 如違，賣者、買者同罪。

translations.literal: If violated, sellers and buyers were punished alike.
translations.idiomatic: Violators were punished alike, whether seller or buyer.

sentences.zh: 僧道服：洪武十四年定，禪僧，茶褐常服，青絛玉色袈裟。

translations.literal: Buddhist and Daoist dress: fixed in Hongwu fourteenth year, Chan monks, tea-brown everyday dress, green sash jade-colored kasaya.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist and Daoist dress was fixed in the fourteenth year of Hongwu. Chan monks wore tea-brown everyday dress and jade-colored kasaya with green sashes.

sentences.zh: 講僧，玉色常服，綠絛淺紅袈裟。

translations.literal: Lecture monks, jade-colored everyday dress, green sash pale-red kasaya.
translations.idiomatic: Lecture monks wore jade-colored everyday dress and pale-red kasaya with green sashes.

sentences.zh: 教僧，皁常服，黑絛淺紅袈裟。

translations.literal: Teaching monks, black everyday dress, black sash pale-red kasaya.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching monks wore black everyday dress and pale-red kasaya with black sashes.

sentences.zh: 僧官如之。

translations.literal: Buddhist officials likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist officials followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 惟僧錄司官袈裟，綠文及環皆飾以金。

translations.literal: Only Buddhist Registry officials' kasaya had green brocade and rings all ornamented with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Only the kasaya of Buddhist Registry officials had green brocade and rings all ornamented with gold.

sentences.zh: 道士，常服青法服，朝衣皆赤，道官亦如之。

translations.literal: Daoist priests, everyday dress blue ritual robes, court dress all red; Daoist officials likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist priests wore blue ritual robes in everyday dress and all-red court dress; Daoist officials followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 惟道錄司官法服、朝服，綠文飾金。

translations.literal: Only Daoist Registry officials' ritual robes and court dress had green brocade ornamented with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Only the ritual robes and court dress of Daoist Registry officials had green brocade ornamented with gold.

sentences.zh: 凡在京道官，紅道衣，金襴，木簡。

translations.literal: All Daoist officials in the capital, red Daoist robes, gold brocade borders, wooden tablets.
translations.idiomatic: All Daoist officials in the capital wore red Daoist robes with gold brocade borders and carried wooden tablets.

sentences.zh: 在外道官，紅道衣，木簡，不用金襴。

translations.literal: Daoist officials outside the capital, red Daoist robes, wooden tablets, not using gold brocade borders.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist officials outside the capital wore red Daoist robes and carried wooden tablets, without gold brocade borders.

sentences.zh: 道士，青道服，木簡。

translations.literal: Daoist priests, blue Daoist robes, wooden tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist priests wore blue Daoist robes and carried wooden tablets.
